articles.headline: England rocked by injury on eve of World Cup
keyFacts: Morgan Smithies has been ruled out of the Rugby League World Cup due to an injury picked up in training.
England head coach Brian McDermott said the team will miss Smithies's work ethic and toughness.
Kallum Watkins will replace Smithies in the England squad and arrive in Perth ahead of the weekend.
body: Rugby League World Cup: England rocked by injury with Perth Bears-bound Morgan Smithies ruled out
Morgan Smithies has been ruled out of the Rugby League World Cup in a blow to England head coach Brian McDermott; he has been replaced by Leeds Rhinos' Kallum Watkins
Wednesday 14 October 2026 14:35, UK
England have been rocked by injury on the eve of the Rugby League World Cup with Perth Bears-bound Morgan Smithies ruled out of the tournament.
Leeds Rhinos' Kallum Watkins is set to depart for Australia to take the place of lock and second-row forward Smithies.
Watkins, who played in two of last year's three Ashes Tests against Australia, will arrive in Perth ahead of the weekend but is not set to feature in Saturday's opener against Tonga.
Head coach Brian McDermott said: "It's really unfortunate what has happened to Morgan with an injury picked up in training.
"Morgan has been great since we entered camp. He's a real team player and his work ethic and toughness are qualities that we will certainly miss.
"Kallum enjoyed a terrific season with Leeds this year and has been part of our England Performance Programme building into this World Cup.
"I look forward to welcoming him into camp as we step up our preparations."

Watkins, 35, started out his glittering career as a centre but has transitioned to the pack in recent years and has played under McDermott at club level during his first stint as a player at Headingley.
Should he feature, he will play in his fourth Rugby League World Cup after previously representing his country on home soil in 2013 and 2022 plus Down Under when England progressed to the 2017 final.

articles.headline: We might not have to wait 13 years for the next GTA
keyFacts: Rockstar technical lead Phil Hooker told Bloomberg that the tools and team built for GTA VI will allow faster future development.
Jennifer Kolbe stated that GTA VI did not cost more than 1.5 billion dollars to develop, denying previous reports.
GTA VI is scheduled to launch on November 19th for the PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X and S.
body: Rockstar Games might not keep fans waiting as long for the next installment of Grand Theft Auto. As part of Bloomberg’s expansive report on the making of GTA VI, Rockstar technical lead Phil Hooker said that the “engine, the tools and the team we’ve built during this project will allow us to do things more quickly.”
We might not have to wait 13 years for the next GTA
Rockstar’s Phil Hooker says the engine, tools, and team the developer has built ‘will allow us to do things more quickly.’
GTA VI had a notoriously long development process. It took eight years to make, leaving a 13-year gap between this upcoming installment and GTA V.

The report points to the one-year gap between Grand Theft Auto III and Grand Theft Auto: Vice City, which was possible because Rockstar already had the framework in place for its next project. “I feel confident that we can build on top of this [GTA VI] and go more sideways than upwards to build more compelling content,” Hooker told Bloomberg.
There were several other interesting details in the report as well, including:

- Rockstar built a studio dedicated to creating nonplayable characters (NPCs) after the team realized it lacked the “production capabilities” needed to write and animate all of the game’s NPCs. That contributed to the game’s delay. “I think when it became apparent that some areas weren’t going to make it, that’s when we decided to make the shift of date,” Hooker said. “We could hit that schedule, but it won’t be the game we want to make.”

- GTA VI apparently didn’t cost more than $1.5 billion to develop, as Rockstar’s publishing head Jennifer Kolbe shut down a report that suggested it was more expensive to build than Dubai’s Burj Khalifa.

- Rockstar head of development Aaron Garbut responded to the massive GTA VI leak in 2022: “It feels like somebody’s wading through your dirty washing,” Garbut told Bloomberg. “It’s like they’re inside your head. You see your early work out there. Nobody’s ever supposed to see that. It’s really weirdly invasive. And so it’s quite hard to deal with on an emotional level.”
- Since 2018, the number of Rockstar employees has risen from 2,441 to 4,711 across 12 offices.
GTA VI launches on November 19th on the PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X | S.

articles.headline: Feyi-Waboso expected to be fit for England's Nations Championship campaign
keyFacts: Immanuel Feyi-Waboso is expected to be fit for England's Nations Championship campaign after a hamstring injury.
Chiefs director of rugby Rob Baxter stated that scans showed minimal damage and the wing should return soon.
England's opening match of the tournament is scheduled against Australia on November 8.
body: Immanuel Feyi-Waboso expected to be fit for England's Nations Championship fixture against Australia in November

Immanuel Feyi-Waboso tweaked hamstring playing for Exeter against Newcastle; wing is on track to feature in England’s opening Nations Championship Test against Australia on November 8; England then play Japan on November 14 and New Zealand on November 21
Wednesday 14 October 2026 13:56, UK
Immanuel Feyi-Waboso is expected to be fit for England's Nations Championship campaign this autumn after receiving a positive update on his hamstring injury.
The explosive wing hobbled off in the second half of Exeter's 34-28 victory over Newcastle last weekend.

Chiefs director of rugby Rob Baxter insists Feyi-Waboso is expected to return sooner rather than later, suggesting he should be available for the opening Nations Championship fixture against Australia on November 8.
Baxter said: "Manny's got some awareness there. The scan doesn't show up too much and on testing he's very good.
"We're hopeful that we can treat the symptoms he's showing and see where he gets to over the next week or so.
"Looking at how he's reporting post-game and (Monday), there's nothing I'm hearing from our physios saying there should be a long-term issue now.
"Seeing that he's reporting so well and he's functionally so good, there may not need to be too much intervention."
Feyi-Waboso has been limited to 16 caps since making his debut two years ago due to a series of injuries including shoulder, hamstring and concussion.
The 23-year-old is one of 25 centrally-contracted players, giving England control over his medical arrangements, and he has already been assessed by one of their physios.
Baxter added: "England like players to go and see certain specialists and we're in a delicate time for both parties.
"We're desperate for Manny to play because we've got some important games and England want him to be able to feature in the autumn.
"Hopefully there won't be any dispute based on where Manny feels he is."

articles.headline: Hyrule Field Sure Feels Empty In Ocarina Of Time These Days
keyFacts: A reviewer explored Hyrule Field in a remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time and found it mostly empty compared to modern open-world games.
The GameSpot reviewer noted that the remake remains faithful to the 1998 original by keeping the field's size and sparse landscape largely unchanged.
The reviewer stated that while the field serves its purpose as a travel hub, it lacks the extensive exploration features seen in newer Zelda titles.
body: The young adventurer Link has been entrusted with an epic quest that will take him to every corner of the globe. He is fated to do incredible things, to become the Hero of Time, but for now he is just a boy. He says farewell to his dearest friend, Saria, and, with his trusty sword and his fairy Navi in tow, he steps out of his tiny community of forest children and finds himself in awe of the wider world. As he gazes out, he realizes this vast untamed wilderness is … maybe the size of a couple of football fields? Thereabouts?

I was there when Ocarina of Time first released in 1998, and like many young gamers, my mind was blown. This was one of our earliest experiences with 3D exploration in an open world, and it truly felt vast. The central hub of Hyrule Field was large enough to gracefully cross on horseback. Almost 30 years later, though, the once-majestic Hyrule Field lacks its original luster.

I recently got to play the Ocarina of Time remake , and like lots of players, I was curious how--or if--Hyrule Field would be updated for this latest incarnation of the game. The answer is that it's very faithful to the original, for better and worse. The size appears roughly the same, and the landscape is mostly empty aside from the spokes leading out from the hub and Lon Lon Ranch at its center. There appear to be a few more irregular hills and rock formations to add realistic texture, but it is largely recognizable.

On one hand, this makes sense. As I mentioned in my preview, this remake aims to respectfully recreate the original Ocarina of Time, and complicating Hyrule Field with a bunch of random stuff wouldn't feel authentic. Your default run speed is a little faster, so it doesn't feel like it's wasting your time crossing an empty field. It mostly exists as a space between the towns and dungeons you visit for quests.

At the same time, we've now seen the Zelda series fully embrace and even innovate modern open-world design with the two most recent core games, Breath of the Wild and Tears of the Kingdom. Those two games created massive wilderness that actually felt, appropriately, wild. They created tons of little hidden nooks and crevices to explore, with environmental and navigation puzzles to solve. One reason those two games have captured so much attention, and became so beloved, is because you can truly spend dozens of hours simply roaming around, exploring, and discovering.

An Ocarina of Time remake was never going to recreate that feeling. Its core design is just too different. But it's hard not to notice, having played the modern Zelda games, that this Hyrule Field is relatively tiny. It's true to the original, but there just isn't much to do. Just how much that impacts your experience will likely depend on what you're looking to get out of the remake.

articles.headline: GTA 6 Leaker Threatens Story Spoilers If Caught
keyFacts: Grand Theft Auto 6 leaker Cyberleek threatened to release game story spoilers if caught by authorities.
Cyberleek stated it will not release the full game build because a crypto donation goal failed.
Grand Theft Auto 6 is scheduled for official release on November 19.
body: Notorious Grand Theft Auto 6 leaker Cyberleek has threatened to reveal story spoilers if the hacking group is caught. In a new post accompanying Cyberleek's latest leaks, the person (or persons) said it has details on the game's ending and considered leaking it to "punish Take-Two greatly."

However, Cyberleek said leaking the ending would ruin the experience for players, and has only published out-of-context clips from the game's final missions so far. Still, don't think that Cyberleek isn't adverse to totally spoiling the game; they said, "the dead man's switch is active" and that story spoilers will be made public if Cyberleek is caught.

The latest unofficial videos of Grand Theft Auto 6 show new hairstyles and Lucia picking up a joint, which goes in her "Cigarettes & Drugs" inventory tab. More clothing customization is shown off, including what might be the first glimpse at the tie-in uniforms the Miami Heat will wear. Clips from what presumably is the final mission, "The End of the Road," are also included. People on Reddit have detailed what's shown if you want to read about the potential spoilers.
Cyberleek's crypto scheme backfired

The rest of Cyberleek's message was about how it will not release the full build of the game after its $30 million crypto goal was not met. Cyberleek previously asked for "a donation" from players, and if those donations reached certain milestones, Cyberleek would release more clips from GTA 6 and eventually the game in its entirety. The clips released were of co-protagonist Lucia naked, because the internet is nothing if not horny. After thirsty folks got their fill, the Cyberleek coin's market cap sharply fell.

"Sad, the negativity — and how few believe anything real is behind this. CL was transparent about the token from day one: a donation, never an investment," Cyberleek said. "It changed nothing — influencers decided the story before the facts arrived. The Edict stands. The leeks stop here. For now."

If Cyberleek sticks to its guns, we won't see any more leaks from it ahead of GTA 6's launch next month on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X. But if Cyberleek is caught by the authorities, like other hacking groups, before the game's launch, it'll be interesting to see if Cyberleek's "dead man's switch" is real or an empty threat.
Grand Theft Auto 6 will be released officially on Nov. 19.

articles.headline: US inflation rises more than expected ahead of midterm elections
keyFacts: US inflation rose to 3.7% in the year to September, exceeding forecasts due to higher gasoline prices.
The data release comes ahead of next month's midterm elections, which are focused on cost of living pressures.
Experts stated the US Federal Reserve will monitor if energy costs drive inflation higher in other areas.
body: - Published
US inflation rose by more than expected in the year to September, according to official figures, in the final data release before the midterm elections next month.
The pace of price rises increased to 3.7%, up from 3.4% in the 12 months to August.
Inflation was above forecasts, driven by higher gasoline prices which have spiked following disruption to Middle East energy supplies due to the US-Israel conflict with Iran.
The elections are being fought over cost of living pressures across the US.
What is inflation?
Inflation is the rate at which the price of products or services increase over time.
For example, if a bottle of milk costs $1 but rises to $1.10 a year later, then annual inflation for bottled milk is 10%.
Officials from the Bureau of Labor Statistics measure inflation through the consumer price index (CPI).
It tracks the price changes of hundreds of day-to-day items including fresh food, gasoline and medical services to work out the overall level of inflation in the US economy.
The bureau updates this so-called basket of goods over time as peoples' spending and lifestyle habits change.
What causes inflation?
There are several factors that can cause inflation to rise.
If demand for a product outstrips its supply, that can lead to producers raising prices - the craze for Labubu dolls in recent years and the high resale prices are an example.
Higher incomes can also lead to higher demand, for example, which in turn pushes up prices.

Supply can also affect inflation. If supply of a product is reduced, but demand remains constant, that can cause prices to rise. A good example of this is crude oil, which is used to make gasoline and diesel.
Before the US-Israel war with Iran began, it was trading at just over $70 a barrel but when the conflict constricted crude supplies, the price quickly rose and is currently over $100.
What is the current rate of inflation?
Inflation has risen to 3.7% in the year to September, which is a higher-than-expected increase fuelled by gasoline prices.
Car fuel prices jumped by 34.2% over 12 months.
In September alone, they jumped by 9.1%, accounting for more than half of the increase in inflation, according to the Bureau or Labor Statistics.
Overall, energy inflation was up by 20.4% over the year as prices for fuel oil, energy services and electricity climbed. Fuel oil, used in home heating, was up 74.2% over the year.

Experts said the US Federal Reserve - which sets the country's interest rate - will be closely watching to see if energy costs begin to affect other areas of the economy, such as food prices, and drive inflation higher.
At the moment, food inflation remains subdued. It was flat over the month of September, and was 2.5% across the year.
Core inflation, which strips out food and energy prices, was 2.6%.
How have tariffs affected inflation?
Since coming into office for the second time, President Donald Trump has introduced tariffs on most US trading partners around the world.
While most of the additional global levies were outlawed by the Supreme Court in February, the president immediately announced a new 10% global tariff to replace them.

Trump argued the tariffs would increase America's tax earnings, boost manufacturing and encourage people to buy US-made goods, but the higher import taxes have also had an impact on inflation, according to research from the Federal Reserve Bank of New York.

Higher tariffs - which are levies that businesses pay on the goods they import - directly raise prices for US companies unless the overseas firms they are buying from lower prices to absorb some of the cost.
In response to the new tariffs, the New York Fed found exporters reduced prices very little, meaning US-based businesses ended up absorbing nearly 90% of the cost of the added tax.
Indirectly, higher tariffs also affected the prices of locally made goods, as many US producers rely on parts or materials from overseas.
Overall, the Fed found that every percentage point increase in average tariffs led to nearly a 0.25% price increase for consumer goods after one year.
Has inflation been worse lately?
While inflation is currently above where the US Federal Reserve would like - it has a target of 2% - it has been much higher in previous years.
During the Covid pandemic, issues such as supply chain disruption started pushing inflation up.
Additionally, in early 2022 when Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine, oil prices surged over $100 a barrel.
Both of these factors helped to drive inflation to a peak of about 9%.
Can inflation ever go down?
It's important to note that if inflation is rising at a slower rate, that does not mean prices are going down - it simply means prices are rising at a slower pace.
A bit of inflation is considered good for an economy as the the Federal Reserve's target rate illustrates.
Many central banks consider inflation of about 2% or a little higher to be stable, and at a level that doesn't impact people's purchasing decisions.
Much below that, people can delay spending if they expect prices to fall further. That can lead to businesses reducing wages, or reducing the number of workers to cope with lower demand.

articles.headline: TSN Archives: 100 Million Miracles Rolled into One! (Nov. 1, 1969, issue)
keyFacts: The New York Mets defeated the Baltimore Orioles in the 66th World Series to become baseball champions.
Thousands of fans celebrated the victory at Shea Stadium by flooding the field, digging up bases, and gouging out turf.
Baltimore manager Earl Weaver praised the Mets after the series, stating that they have pitching, defense, and timely hitting.
body: This story by managing editor Lowell Reidenbaugh originally appeared in the Nov. 1, 1969, issue of The Sporting News under the headline “100 Million Miracles Rolled into One!” after the “Miracle Mets” defeated the Orioles in the World Series.
The hands on the huge Longines clock atop the scoreboard stood at 3:16 p. m. on October 16.
The big birds out of LaGuardia zoomed overhead in a kind of ceremonial roar.
And the little birds dipped and darted drunkenly about Shea Stadium as though they had spent the afternoon nipping at fermented mash.

Below, on what was once a neatly manicured playing field, thousands of delirious devotees of baseball screamed their hymns of praise for the New York Mets, the new, and incredible, champions of the baseball universe.

Seconds earlier, the laws of improbability had been rent asunder and the Mets enthroned as baseball's No. 1 team. The one-time symbols of ten-thumbed ineptitude had defeated the Baltimore Orioles, 5 to 8 favorites, in the 66th World Series and now their bug-eyed partisans were engaging in a harvest ritual.
TSN ARCHIVES: Why even President Nixon thinks Tom Seaver can save the Mets (Oct. 11, 1969)
It was the third such demonstration in 23 days. On September 24, they celebrated the clinching of first place in the National League's East Division.
On October 6, they repeated when the Mets won the league's championship series with the Atlanta Braves, who were the Best in the West.
Home Plate Disappears

And now they were at it again, only this time they yelled louder and longer. They displayed more banners, signs like “We're No. 1,” “Cortland State Loves Nancy Seaver” and “The Mets Are World Champions.”
They scribbled success slogans on the outfield walls, they ripped away the three bases and dug up home plate.
And, of course, they gouged out huge chunks of turf where lately had trod such spiked idols as Jerry Koosman, Donn Clendenon, Cleon Jones, Al Weis and Ron Swoboda.

Shea Stadium was not the only scene of wild rejoicing in New York. Veteran observers of Gotham celebrations said they'd never seen anything to top this one, including the return of Charles A. Lindbergh after his New York-to-Paris flight in 1927, V-J Day in 1945 and the welcome for the Astronauts in 1969.
TSN ARCHIVES: The secret to Cy Youngs 511 wins, in his own words (April 17, 1971)
In baseball's first 100 years, there was nothing to compare with the spectacular rise of the Mets.
The 1914 Braves' Series sweep over the lordly Philadelphia Athletics? Strictly second rate.
The Little Miracle of Coogan's Bluff in 1951? Forget it.
They All Remember

This was a hundred-million miracles rolled into one and, young as many of the celebrants were, they were not so youthful they could not remember how the Mets had languished in tenth place the first four years of their existence, then risen to ninth, fallen to tenth again and climbed to ninth before a second expansion program forged two six-club divisions and brought the Mets to the peak of affluence.
While the multitudes shouted and screamed, those who had fashioned the implausible blockbuster were whooping it up as though each had suddenly become $15,000 richer, which he had.
With champagne shampoos and ear-splitting shrieks, they toasted and teased one another in calculated tumult.
TSN ARCHIVES: Bob Gibson’s record-breaking 1968 might be the GOAT pitching season (Oct. 19, 1968)
Ron Swoboda, who drove in the title-clinching run and sparkled with his glove in the fourth game, shouted, “We're the saints of lost causes,” (St. Jude, please take note.)
Cleon Jones, who scored the deciding run, added: “Some people may not believe in us, but then, too, some people still believe the world is flat.”
Added Ed Charles, a key figure in the Mets' second-game victory: “This is the summit. We're No. I, and you just can't get any bigger than this.”
Gil Hodges found it difficult to compare the 1969 Mets with other world champions he had known as a player, the 1955 Brooklyn Dodgers and the 1959 Los Angeles Dodgers.
“It's the same and it's different,” said the former first baseman. “As a player and as a manager, it's different—it's hard to explain. I'm so proud of them all.”
Without naming names, Hodges had to be thinking of personalities like Clendenon. Last spring he was a cause celebre in a tug of war between the Astros and Expos.
Big Year for Donn
Traded by Montreal to Houston, the one-time law student announced his retirement from baseball to accept an executive position with a pen company in Atlanta.
Commissioner Bowie Kuhn ordered Donn back to Montreal, which sent two other players to Houston in the big first baseman's place.
On June 15, the trading deadline, Clendenon was sold to the Mets. He batted .248 for the season, hitting 16 homers and batting in 51 runs.
In the Series, the 34-year-old giant clouted three home runs and was named the most valuable player in the classic.

Hodges had to be thinking, too, of Weis, his platooned second baseman, who batted .215 for the season, with two homers and 23 RBIs. In the Series, Weis batted .455, driving in the winning run in the second game and scoring the tying marker with a round-tripper in the final contest.

Hodges had to be thinking of Tommie Agee's two picture catches in the third game, Swoboda's diving stab in the fourth contest, the dependable performances of catcher Jerry Grote, shortstop Bud Harrelson, left Fielder Jones and the Mets' remarkable pitching.
Ah, yes, the pitching
Skimpy Hit Total

The team that won the American League East title with 109 wins and batted ,266, ranking fourth in the majors, collected a record low of only 23 safeties in the five games. They made six hits in the first game, which they won, and then in successive losses, registered only two, four, six and five hits respectively.

From the fourth inning of the first game, when Don Buford hit a double, until the third inning of the fifth encounter, when Dave McNally hit a home run, the Orioles did not make a single extra-base hit. Their extra-base collection for the Series consisted of one double and three homers.

Jerry Koosman, in winning two games, yielded seven hits; Tom Seaver, winning and losing one, allowed 12 hits, and Gary Gentry, who won the third contest, allowed three in six and two-thirds innings. The only other Baltimore safety was off Nolan Ryan, who pitched two and one-third shutout innings in relief.
The Met staff's earned-run average for the five games was 1,80; the Orioles' 2.72.

In winning four consecutive games after losing the opener, the Mets duplicated a feat last performed by the 1942 St. Louis Cardinals, who swept the New York Yankees off their feet. The only other club to turn the trick was the 1915 Boston Red Sox, who eliminated the Phillies.
If much of the baseball public wished to attribute the Met success to luck, Earl Weaver, Baltimore manager, refused to share the opinion.
“They're not lucky, they're a good ball club,” Weaver insisted. “You guys have been saying they are gremlins,” he told newsmen.
Super Hill Staff
“But let's face it. They have pitching and they have defense and they get hitting when they need it. I can tell you this—no other pitching staff contained us so well this season.”
Weaver said he thought the Red Sox and Tigers had better hitting than the Mets, but insisted that the Mets were a stronger club.
He said he'll be rooting for the Mets to win again in 1970.
“Revenge?” someone asked.
“You gotta,” Weaver replied. “It's always discouraging when you lose.”

“We're not shocked at losing, not by any means,” said Brooks Robinson, who gathered only one single in 19 at-bats. “We have nothing to be ashamed of. We didn't underestimate them. They just played better than we did.”
The Orioles' other Robinson, Frank, who had three hits in 16 tries, said he was not stunned, “just a little disappointed” at the outcome.

As the Orioles pulled themselves together for the somber return trip to Baltimore—a junket so many had expected them to make in triumph—and the Mets prepared for a winter of idolization, one observer recalled a brief tableau in Atlanta just 12 days earlier.
A Wild Forecast
The Mets had defeated the Braves, 9-5 in the first game of the Championship Series, scoring five runs in the eighth inning against knuckleballer Phil Niekro.

Just inside the Met clubhouse after the game, a visitor found Dave Grote, National League publicity director, in conversation with Yogi Berra, Met coach, and a long-time associate of victory in his years with the Yankees.
“I was just telling Yogi,” Grote volunteered, “that I'm convinced the Mets are sure to goal) the way. After the way they played today, nothing's going to stop them.”
The prognostication seemed unworthy even of Jeanne Dixon at the time. On October 16, it seemed worthy of Nostradamus.

articles.headline: DayZ Badlands DLC release countdown: Exact date and time
keyFacts: Developers Bohemia Interactive announced that the DayZ Badlands DLC releases worldwide on Thursday, October 15.
The expansion introduces the 267 square-kilometer Nasdara province map, featuring desert survival, faction conflicts, and new arsenal additions.
Players can wishlist the upcoming downloadable content on Steam ahead of its scheduled launch.
body: DayZ Badlands DLC is coming to the base game, and we will have a new map to uncover. This will be the biggest update for the game this year, and we don’t have to wait long to try it out.
Before we can put our foot on the map of Nasdara province, let’s find out when the expansion goes live.
Table of contents
DayZ Badlands DLC release countdown
What to expect from DayZ Badlands DLC
DayZ Badlands DLC release countdown

The Badlands DLC goes live worldwide on Thursday, October 15 . The release date and time have been announced in advance by developers Bohemia Interactive, and I’m not expecting any changes this late. The following countdown will expire once the game goes live.
Hurry Up!
The countdown is based on the following times.
3am PDT
5am CDT
6am EDT
10am UTC
11am BST
12pm CEST
What to expect from DayZ Badlands DLC

Badlands DLC brings desert survival to the popular zombie title as we take our first steps into the Nasdara province. This is a sun-scorched expanse with a lot of sand and cracked soil to test you. Not only will you have to survive the stragglers, but the rugged terrain and scanty resources will make things harder for you.

The new map is 267 sq.km long, with sands on one side and jagged border mountains on the other. This is also a piece of land plagued by geopolitical trouble. Expect to find constant conflicts between the factions that want to seize control. You will come across historical sites, Middle Eastern-style cities, and crumbling Soviet-era military installations all around the map.
Hence, survival will not be easy at all. However, you’ll find plenty of loot and lore to discover. The new map also brings fresh additions to the arsenal that you can enjoy.
While there’s no pre-order available with the DLC, you can wishlist it on Steam to stay on top of the launch.

keyFacts: Houthis launched missile attacks across Saudi Arabia, sparking a limited fire at Aramco headquarters and causing four injuries from debris in Riyadh, Saudi authorities said.
The International Committee of the Red Cross warned that Yemen's hospitals are at capacity due to escalating fighting and war injuries.
The IMF warned that attacks on Saudi Arabia could impact people everywhere by causing economic concerns and disrupting energy markets, IMF head Kristalina Georgieva said.
body: What you need to know
- Fire breaks out at Aramco headquarters in Dhahran
- Four injured because of debris in Saudi capital Riyadh
- Fuel facility in Sanaa hit by Saudi-led coalition forces
Here's the latest on the Saudi-Houthi conflict and elsewhere in the Middle East on Wednesday, October 14, 2026:

Red Cross warns that Yemen's hospitals are at capacity

The International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) has cautioned that Yemen's hospitals are finding it difficult to cope with the skyrocketing amount of war injuries as fighting intensifies across the country.
Small hospitals in front-line areas in Marib and Taiz are seeing some 700 casualties of the conflict in a single week, a far great number than their usual amount of patients.
"Trauma care staff are under enormous pressure," ICRC health coordinator Feras Abusamra said in a statement.
Only a handful of hospitals in Yemen are capable of handling intensive care patients, and even those lack many of the necessary supplies and medicines as other health facilities across the country.

At least 200,000 people have been displaced in the conflict, further complicating matters for Yemen's still-functional hospitals. Moreover, due to changing front lines on multiple fronts, international organizations say at least 800,000 people have become cut off from much-needed humanitarian aid.
Riyadh residents report explosions
Civilians in the Saudi capital Riyadh reported hearing an explosion above their city as the govenment claimed in intercepted a ballistic missile launched from Yemen.
The Houthis then claimed they had again struck Riyadh airport as well as an Aramco oil refinery, something Saudi authorities have not confirmed.
The increase in attacks on Saudi soil has increased pressure on Riyadh's allies, including the United States, to evaluate whether they should join the coalition against the Houthis more directly.
IMF warns attacks on Saudi could impact people "everywhere"

The recent attacks on Saudi Arabia could affect people adversely "everywhere," as conflict in the energy-rich region could lead to a range of economic concerns, International Monetary Fund (IMF) head Kristalina Georgieva said Wednesday.

The escalation between the Houthis and Saudi Arabia has sparked fears of aggravating global crises that could impact global growth, with energy markets already disrputed due to the ongoing conflict between Iran and the US.
"The Saudi economy is important for the region and the world," IMF managing director Georgieva said at a news conference during the Annual Meetings of the Fund and World Bank in Bangkok.
"In that sense, these developments have potentially negative spillovers for everybody, everywhere," she said.
Aramco offices catches fire after suspected Houthi attack
Saudi Arabia said that an attack on the headquarters of oil state oil firm Aramco sparked a "limited fire."
The fire at the building at Aramco's complex in the eastern city of Dhahran resulted in no casualties or deaths, the country's Energy Ministry said.
A company source told the Reuters news agency that a ballistic missile struck the top floors of an office building.
The complex in Dhahran serves as a major operation for Aramco, which is the world's largest oil company.
Hours earlier, Saudi authorities said they had intercepted several missiles, including over the capital city Riyadh.
Several injured by fallen missile debris in Riyadh
Four people were injured as a result of falling debris following two intercepted Houthi missile attacks, Saudi authorities said.
According to the country's civil defense agency, two women, a man and a child were injured in the capital Riyadh, with 15 homes suffering damage.
This came after residents heard a powerful explosion in the Saudi capital, with an alert being sent to their phones warning of a "hostile aerial threat."
Saudi-led coalition strikes Sanaa fuel facility
The Saudi-led coalition fighting the Houthis struck targets in the Yemeni capital of Sanaa on Tuesday, Houthi-run broadcaster Al Masirah said.

Locals reported hearing strong explosions in the city hours after a coalition spokesperson urged people to leave the all-Suhaba fuel facility, which belongs to the Yemeni Oil Company, and a nearby site ahead of a strike.
According to a coalition spokesperson, the Houthis were using the facility for storing missiles and drones. The facility is located on a hill overlooking Sanaa.
The company said the storage facilities at the site were empty, with a strike not affecting oil reserves or supplies to residents.
Welcome to our coverage
We will be following all the latest updates from the escalation between Saudi Arabia and Yemen-based militant group, the Houthis.
The compound of energy company Aramco saw a fire break out, the Saudi Ministry of Energy said. Saudi authorities also reported four injuries as a result of missile debris falling over Riyadh.
Meanwhile, the Saudi-led coalition fighting the Houthis in Yemen continued its strikes on Tuesday by targeting oil facilities west of capital Sanaa, the local Houthi-run broadcaster said.

articles.headline: Ukraine says SpaceX’s Starshield throttling hampers defense against Russian strikes on energy sites
keyFacts: Ukrainian officials said speed limits imposed without warning on SpaceX military-grade Starshield terminals disrupted military missions and drone operations.
Serhii Beskrestnov, an adviser to Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky, warned that the restrictions could undermine air defenses against Russian drone strikes.
Neither SpaceX nor CEO Elon Musk has publicly confirmed the reported speed restrictions on the terminals.
body: Ukrainian officials said speed limits were imposed on military-grade Starlink terminals without warning, disrupting military missions and forcing the cancellation of some drone operations.

Serhii Beskrestnov, an adviser to Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky on defense technology, said the restrictions apply to Starshield, SpaceX’s military service, and limit terminals moving at speeds above 100 mph. Starshield satellites feature enhanced encryption and advanced security features, and are owned and controlled by the U.S. Department of War .
“Our defense forces received no warning,” Beskrestnov wrote , adding that the restrictions had disrupted several missions.

Ukraine told SpaceX that the speed restriction “was not in place for our terminals previously, and its introduction has created significant operational challenges for Ukrainian users,” according to a person familiar with the matter.
Beskrestnov warned that the restrictions could undermine Ukraine’s air defenses, particularly interceptor units used to counter Russian Shahed drones.
“In effect, through their actions, our partners are depriving us of one of the few options available to defend the country against jet-powered Shaheds,” Beskrestnov said.

He also said that the restriction was connected to current political tensions, as Zelensky and President Donald Trump , a close ally of SpaceX CEO Elon Musk , have sparred over an energy ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine.
“Clearly, this action is no coincidence and is linked to the current political situation,” Beskrestnov wrote.
Neither SpaceX nor Musk has publicly confirmed the reported restrictions. SpaceX did not respond to a request for comment from the Washington Examiner .
The reported move has drawn criticism from European officials.
Polish Foreign Minister Radosław Sikorski called out Musk in a social media post , asking whether he was “playing politics with your products again” and warning that European customers were watching.

The dispute comes as Russia and Ukraine continue to trade attacks despite Trump’s announcement of an energy ceasefire. Trump said Sunday on Truth Social that the two countries had agreed to halt attacks on energy infrastructure, offering few details while warning both sides not to violate the agreement.
Zelensky said Moscow has disregarded the proposed ceasefire, saying Ukraine would continue retaliatory strikes unless Russia formally agreed to stop attacking its energy infrastructure.

Russian attacks continued Wednesday, with Ukrainian presidential adviser Dmytro Lytvyn saying Kyiv had received no advance warning from allies for a second consecutive day. Ukraine’s air force also said it received no alerts before the first series of overnight ballistic missile strikes.
Zelensky said Russia launched 39 ballistic missiles and more than 120 drones and loitering munitions against energy and critical infrastructure in Kyiv and the surrounding region.
He described the strikes as a deliberate attack on infrastructure covered by Trump’s proposed ceasefire and urged Washington to increase pressure on Moscow.

Zelensky called on Trump to impose stronger sanctions on Russia and provide Ukraine with additional Patriot air defense systems, arguing that greater military and economic pressure was necessary to bring the war to an end.
REPUBLICAN BACKLASH BREWS OVER TRUMP’S DIESEL DEAL WITH RUSSIA
“Peace can come only through strength,” Zelensky said .

In September 2022, Musk ordered SpaceX engineers to shut down Starlink satellite coverage in parts of Ukraine during a counteroffensive over fears that Ukraine’s offensive could spark Russian nuclear retaliation. The shutdown caused communication blackouts and disrupted Ukrainian military operations for hours.

articles.headline: The Legend Of Zelda: Ocarina Of Time Remake’s Latest Trailer Shows A Lot Of Old, But Some Surprising New
keyFacts: Nintendo's upcoming remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time for the Switch 2 features a new location called the Hall of Fallen Foes.
The new room functions as a museum where players can view defeated enemies, read descriptions, and replay boss battles with time tracking.
The remake launches on November 5 as part of the series' 40th anniversary, followed by a live-action film next year.
body: Nintendo’s upcoming remake ofÂ The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time sure does look like a faithful recreation of the Nintendo 64 classic, and most of its latest trailer leans into that by showing the prettier versions of old locales and boss fights Link will make his way through when the remake launches on Switch 2 early next month. However, it also reveals one new thing that will be added in the remake: the Hall of Fallen Foes.

This space looks something like a museum Link can visit that features statues of enemies he’s defeated over the course of the game. Examining these statues will give you a description of the featured monster, perhaps providing some new insight into its behaviors and place in the world, as well as telling you where you can find them again if you want to slap them around for fun. That’s all well and good, but the real draw here is that each of the game’s boss monsters will also be depicted in the Hall of Fallen Foes, and if you want to fight them again, you can do so from this room. The game will also keep track of your best time, so if you want to chase a new personal record, it looks like you’ll be able to take on the game’s bosses as many times as you like.

Ocarina of Time is coming to Switch 2 on November 5, and is the big tentpole game for the series’ 40th anniversary. Next year, Nintendo and Sony are putting out a live-action film starring Benjamin Evan Ainsworth and Bo Bragason as Link and Zelda respectively, though it still hasn’t shown a full trailer of the film yet.

articles.headline: Cisco, Nvidia team up to build fatter, faster pluggable
keyFacts: Cisco and Nvidia developed a new ultra-dense small form factor pluggable optic designed to pack up to eight times the bandwidth of existing pluggables into a single port.
Cisco announced that Microsoft is using its Silicon One P200 routing chips to distribute AI workloads across multiple datacenters.
Cisco announced plans to roll out support for its Live Protect platform in the SONiC network operating system next year.
body: AI datacenters are a rats nest of fiber optic cables stitching together thousands of AI accelerators, NICs, switches, and everything else required to train and run the latest and greatest modes. Cisco hopes to untangle this mess with a new pluggable optic developed in collaboration with Nvidia that will pack between four and eight times the bandwidth of existing pluggables into a single port. Announced at the Open Compute Project (OCP) global summit this week, the ultra-dense small form factor pluggable (USFP) promises to pack up to 32, 400 Gbps lanes into a pluggable roughly the size of existing OSFP modules. Each of these pluggables would boast 12.8 Tbps of Ethernet bandwidth, as much as a high-end enterprise switch just a few years ago. To put that in perspective, the most sophisticated pluggable optics today cap out at around 1.6 Tbps using eight 200 Gbps links. Such a pluggable has the potential to significantly simplify cabling across AI datacenters where it isn't uncommon for each GPU to be paired with an 800 Gbps and soon 1.6 Tbps NIC. A single USFP pluggable could consolidate eight GPUs worth of cabling into a single fiber optic bundle. Meanwhile, on the switch side, a future 204.8 Tbps switch would only require 16 USFP ports to support 128 1.6 Tbps endpoints. Cramming all that connectivity into a single pluggable won't be easy. Today a high-end pluggable optic might pull on the order of 20 watts. Cisco's USFP spec calls for up to 100 watts per pluggable. There are also design constraints that have to be taken into consideration. Four times as many links per pluggable means 4x as many electrical contacts that have to be perfectly seated. Because of this Cisco says USFP modules will employ a two phase insertion mechanism in which the pluggable is first inserted into the cage and then a second mechanism is actuated to make the electrical connection. Speaking of reliability, USFP would have a bigger blast radius than conventional pluggables. A single bad laser or digital signal processor (DSP) has the potential to take out far more than a single GPU, but entire systems. While that might sound bad, it's nothing compared to co-packed or near-package optics where one failure could drop an entire rack's worth of accelerators from the network. Nvidia's participation in the development of the USFP standard is notable as the Ethernet networking titan has largely moved away from pluggables in its most recent set of switches. Many of its Spectrum-X and Quantum-X switches now use co-packaged optics and for good reason. Cutting out the pluggables on the switch side nets a roughly 30 percent power savings. But while Nvidia's latest switches may use CPO, its NICs still rely on pluggables in part because it offers integrators greater flexibility. Not everyone is building 100,000-plus GPU clusters for training. For racks utilizing a top of rack switch, lower power direct attach copper cabling can be used without much issue. Given Nvidia's investments in CPO we can only speculate on its interests in USFP, but it likely comes down to densification. The AI infrastructure giant is rapidly moving toward 600 kW racks packing 144 GPUs on board. First teased in early 2025, Nvidia's Vera Rubin Ultra platform promised 115.2 TB/s scale out bandwidth per rack or about 3.2-6.4 Tbps of bandwidth per GPU package depending on whether they're counting bidirectional bandwidth or not. It just so happens that Cisco's initial USFP spec calls for 16, 400 Gbps links per pluggable, or about 6.4 Tbps of bandwidth. While Cisco and Nvidia may be leading the charge on the development of an ultra dense optical pluggable, like most things Ethernet, USFP will be an open standard anyone can use in their designs. Microsoft taps Cisco for multi-datacenter AI Alongside Cisco's latest tie up with Nvidia, Switchzilla also revealed that Microsoft is now using its Silicon One P200 routing chips to distribute workloads across multiple datacenters. Nvidia and others have taken to calling this kind of multi-site computing: scale across networking. We discussed Cisco's datacenter-scale routing platform at length late last year, but the silicon competes directly with products like Nvidia's Spectrum-XGS and Broadcom's Jericho 4-based offerings. Cisco touts the P200 as the first 51.2 Tbps systems "deployed in a production environment by leading hyperscalers." With enough qualifiers you can be the first at anything. As we reported at the time, Microsoft was among the first major hyperscalers to embrace scale-across networking as a means of overcoming local power constraints with its Fairwater clusters in Wisconsin and Georgia. And it seems we finally know the hardware good old Redmond is using to stitch them together. Cisco gives SONiC some love Speaking of hyperscalers, one thing you probably won't find in a hyperscale network is Cisco's Nexus network operating system (NOS). Hyperscalers like Microsoft typically employ vendor agnostic NOS platforms to avoid vendor lock-in and make managing networks across multiple Ethernet vendors cheaper and easier. Originally developed by Microsoft and later open sourced, SONiC is among the most popular and widely deployed of the hyperscale NOSes. SONiC support, we should note is nothing new for Cisco which contrary to popular belief is more than willing to sell you any one piece of its networking stack, assuming you've got a big enough purse — the hyperscalers certainly do. As such Cisco is one of the biggest contributors to the SONiC project. Instead of forcing customers to use its software stack, Cisco's approach to SONiC and the hyperscale is to extend the NOSes capabilities to better take advantage of ASIC's unique capabilities and allow for integration with its services. At OCP this week, Cisco announced support for its Live Protect platform in SONiC to make it easier for customers to keep up with security patches in the wild. This capacity is expected to roll out next year. ®

articles.headline: The biggest misconceptions about web browsers and why they matter in the AI era
keyFacts: TechRadar reports that while many users blame browsers for tracking, data collection actually comes from websites, advertisers, and third-party scripts.
The article notes that browser AI assistants do not automatically access all tabs, meaning users can restrict AI visibility to specific tasks.
The publication explains that security prevents malicious activity and unauthorized access, while privacy controls what information is collected, shared, and retained.
body: Most people spend more time in their browser than in almost any other piece of software they use. It's where they read the news, check their bank accounts, work, shop and more. Yet, for something so central to daily life, most people have a surprisingly limited understanding of what their browser is actually doing behind the scenes.
Head of Security at Opera.

That gap was easier to overlook when browsers had a relatively simple job. They opened websites and displayed them on a screen. But today, browsers hold login credentials, manage permissions, block trackers and increasingly give AI agents the ability to act on a user's behalf. The browser has gone from being a window on the internet to one of the most important layers between people and everything they do online.

That shift is understandably enough to make users more cautious than they used to be when online. But, misunderstandings about browsers means that caution may be misdirected. Many users make decisions about tools based on outdated assumptions, shaping everything. Users make very different from what they install to what they let an AI feature access.
As the browser takes on more responsibility, understanding what it actually does is becoming a basic part of staying safe online. Here are three common misconceptions worth clearing up.
1. The browser is tracking everything users do

The browser is the interface through which almost everything online happens. So, when people see ads following them around the internet or notice that a website seems to know something about them, it's natural to assume the browser itself is responsible.
But seeing someone's activity isn't the same as the browser collecting, storing or monetizing it.

In most cases, the data collection comes from websites, advertising technology, embedded trackers and third-party scripts, not the browser itself. A single website can have dozens of companies collecting information about a visitor's behavior, even though the user may have no idea those companies are present.

With that in mind, the browser can actually be one of the most transparent parts of the ecosystem. It's the layer that can show users when a website wants access to their location, expose cookie controls and privacy settings, block trackers, and flag potentially dangerous connections.
Those protections don't mean browsers are inherently private, but the browser is often the place where users have the clearest opportunity to see and control what's happening.

That doesn’t mean every browser handles this the same way. Different browsers make different decisions about which protections are enabled by default, what information they expose to users, and how much control they give people over their data. So the browser isn’t necessarily the source of the privacy problem, but it is often one of the most important places to address it. That distinction becomes even more important as AI moves into the browser.
2. AI assistants inside browsers automatically see everything

People sometimes assume that giving an AI assistant access to one part of their browsing experience means giving it access to everything else. But browser access doesn't have to be all or nothing. An AI can be given access to a specific page, tab or task without being given unrestricted visibility into everything else the user has open.

A useful comparison here is employee privilege. No serious organization would give a new hire the keys to every system on day one, or leave that access in place permanently after a project ends. AI assistants inside a browser should be treated the same way. An AI drafting an email should only need access to the email tab, not the banking session running in another window. And when the task ends, access should end with it.

The practical implication for security teams is that AI browser features deserve the same scrutiny as any other tool touching sensitive data. That means asking vendors what the default permissions are, whether access is scoped to a task or granted broadly, and whether users are meaningfully informed about what the AI is doing on their behalf.

The overarching takeaway is that "AI is inside the browser" and "AI has access to everything in the browser" are not the same. Confusing the two is how users end up giving away more than they intended.
3. Privacy and security are the same thing
People often use "privacy" and "security" interchangeably, but they describe two different problems.
Security is primarily about preventing unauthorized access or stopping malicious activity. Privacy is about controlling what information is collected, shared and retained.

Anonymity is a good example of this. More anonymity can mean better privacy because less of a user’s activity can be traced back to them. But take anonymity too far and it can work against security, making malicious activity harder to identify and stop. The two aren’t necessarily opposites, but they aren’t interchangeable either, and maximizing one can sometimes come at the expense of the other.

The same idea also applies to AI tools. An AI feature can be highly secure, with encryption, sandboxing and carefully designed permissions, and still raise privacy concerns if a user’s prompts or page content are sent to a third-party AI provider. At the same time, an AI system can be highly private by running entirely on a user’s device and still create a security risk if a hostile webpage can manipulate it into taking an action the user never intended.

The better option is to ask two separate questions of any browser or feature. First, is my browser safe enough to protect me from malicious activity? And second, does my browser enable me to control the data I’m giving to other companies? A good browser answers yes to both.

The common theme running through all three misconceptions is that browsers have outgrown the way we talk about them. And they’re not done evolving. So, the better we understand where the real privacy and security risks live, and just as importantly where they don't, the better equipped users and organizations will be to make informed decisions about the tools they trust.

articles.headline: U.S. Soccer to launch Arthur M. Blank Crest Cup for women's clubs; initial prize pool set at $1.5 million
keyFacts: U.S. Soccer announced the launch of the Arthur M. Blank Crest Cup, featuring an initial $1.5 million prize pool for women's clubs.
Teams from the NWSL and the Gainbridge Super League will participate in the inaugural tournament, with potential for lower-division and amateur teams to join later.
U.S. Soccer intends to launch the competition by the 2031 Women's World Cup and plans to schedule matches midweek.
body: U.S. Soccer will launch the Arthur M. Blank Crest Cup, a first-of-its-kind women's competition in the country that will see clubs across different leagues compete with each other for a prize pool of $1.5 million.

There is currently no start date for the Crest Cup, but U.S. Soccer intends to have the competition up and running by the 2031 Women's World Cup, which will likely be hosted jointly by the U.S., Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica. Teams from the NWSL and the Gainbridge Super League will take part in the inaugural edition of the event, though other clubs could join the fold at some point.

"It'll for sure be the NWSL teams and the GSL teams and we're looking at the option for lower division professional teams being able to join, as well as amateur women's teams being able to join and what that could and should look like but we're also not of the thought that the tournament can't evolve," U.S. Soccer president Cindy Parlow Cone told select members of the media this week. "Maybe we start with the NWSL and GSL, and then evolve and engage the other teams, right?"

The tournament will resemble the Lamar Hunt U.S. Open Cup, the century-old men's club competition, and other similar cup competitions around the world such as the FA Cup. Parlow Cone admitted she had a longtime interest in launching a women's equivalent in the U.S. and has finally been able to follow through with the idea because of the increasingly robust nature of women's club soccer at the professional and amateur levels nationwide.

"I have wanted to launch this competition for quite some time," Parlow Cone said. "Historically, we haven't had a robust women's amateur league and competition and a number of teams in order to do it and we only had the one Division One professional league, so it didn't seem like the right time then and now GSL has come in as another Division One league and as they get the first couple of years under their belt, I feel like now we're going to also help grow amateur women's soccer in our country so it felt like the right time. Also, as we gear up for the World Cup in 2031, I think this is great timing in order to create another competition."
As with the Open Cup, the Crest Cup winner will be able to qualify for the Concacaf W Champions Cup, broadening experiences for players and staff alike.

"Most of the players and the coaches and the teams in our ecosystem, they only get that international exposure if they make their national teams or if they're lucky, one or two teams, to be able to play in the Concacaf tournament but this is another way to get more players interleague competition that could then lead to international competition in really meaningful games, right?" she said. "Because single elimination, you got to perform on the given day or you're eliminated and then hopefully around the corner, this leads to being able to play in the Women's Club World Cup."

It is likely that Crest Cup games will take place midweek, in between the weekend games that usually take up the calendar in the NWSL and the GSL, but Parlow Cone said it was too early to say definitively. Finding spots on the schedule to play Crest Cup games will be among U.S. Soccer's biggest challenges since player load is changing at the highest levels of the game. In the last two years alone, the inaugural editions of the Concacaf W Champions Cup and the FIFA Women's Champions Cup have been staged, while FIFA also intends to introduce a Women's Club World Cup. The latter competition is reportedly slated to take place in the U.S. in the winter of 2028, according to the Guardian, only adding to the new types of games players might face.

On the flip side, players outside the NWSL run the risk of playing too few games - the 2026 GSL season, for example, runs from August to November and will only feature 14 regular-season matches. Parlow Cone said she is working in collaboration with both the NWSL and the GSL to find the right spots on the calendar while taking player load into consideration.

"I'm a former player so this is always top of mind for me specifically," she said. "I've said it several times. We could not be working more closely with NWSL and GSL and their sporting leaders to create models for the schedules for the exact reason that you mentioned and we want to make sure that we're not overloading the players, not underloading and allowing enough recovery between their league matches and the Crest Cup matches so like I said before, I would imagine that this would be mostly midweek matches but I'm not gonna declaratively say that right now. We're not announcing a launch date, I'm definitely not telling you what day of the week we're gonna play the matches quite yet."

articles.headline: Big scorelines, one-sided games - are Women's World Cup play-offs working?
keyFacts: Top European teams recorded heavy aggregate wins against lower-ranked opponents in the Women's World Cup qualifying play-offs.
England manager Sarina Wiegman stated that Uefa will review whether the current qualification structure works or needs to change.
England will play a two-legged tie against Ukraine in the next stage of the qualification process.
body: - Published
The ease in which England saw off Greece in round one of the Women's World Cup qualifying play-offs showed just how inefficient the structure currently is.
The two-time European champions were superior in every sense as they won 8-1 on aggregate against a Greece side ranked 55 places lower in the world.
Realistically, Greece stood little chance in a two-legged tie against Sarina Wiegman's side despite performing well in their home 3-1 defeat.
England's resounding victory was not a one-off as Europe's other top nations, who were forced to drop into the play-offs, also met lower-ranked opposition and won emphatically.
It was not an evening that truly reflects the growth of European women's football, which has become more competitive than ever in recent years.
It was, however, indicative that the qualification process perhaps needs reviewing by Uefa.
Why did we see heavy scorelines?
One of the main reasons for Tuesday night's results was that only one team from the league phase groups received automatic qualification.
The Netherlands, 2017 European champions, finished second in their group behind France, ranked sixth in the world. They went on to beat Hungary 11-0 on aggregate.
Norway, World Cup winners in 1995 and six-time European finalists, lost out to giants Germany in their group and ended up beating Romania 8-0.
Other League A fallouts Sweden and the Republic of Ireland thrashed their opponents 15-0 and 12-0 respectively.

So it was no surprise when back-to-back European champions England, who were drawn in the same group as world champions Spain, went on to record another heavy victory against much weaker opposition from League C in their play-off.
"Of course we wanted to qualify straight away, that's not the case," said England manager Wiegman when asked about the qualification process again on Tuesday.
"For us now, the facts are that we are in the play-offs, we have played Greece, now we're through, and now we're going to play Ukraine. That's what my focus is on.
"Uefa will review how things are set up and see whether they think it works or it should be better, or different. I don't think it's my place now to review that."
The Lionesses still have another two-legged tie against Ukraine to play, with the first leg taking place away from home on 1 December and the return fixture at Wembley Stadium on 5 December.
Ukraine are a side who England beat twice in the league phase by an aggregate score of 9-1.
It seems absurd that they should have to beat the same team on at least three occasions as part of their qualification process.
England have won seven of their last eight qualifying matches, scoring 21 goals, conceding just six times, and their only defeat was away from home against world champions Spain.
They came runners-up in League A3 only on their head-to-head record with the best team in the world - they even beat Spain 1-0 at Wembley.
England's overall tally of 15 points in the league phase was beaten by just three other teams - Germany, Switzerland and Hungary.
Switzerland and Hungary were also in qualifying groups in League B and League C that did not include a single team from the world's top 45 ranked nations.
In contrast England, who were seeded in League A, had Iceland - ranked 13th - as a tricky opponent, and world number one Spain in their four-team group.
Is the competition good enough?
When qualifying for the 2023 Women's World Cup, England beat Latvia on two occasions, winning 20-0 and 10-0 .
That tournament saw an increase from 24 to 32 teams and while qualification was still one-sided, the showpiece in Australia and New Zealand was a different story.

England were tested against debutants Haiti in the group stages, narrowly winning 1-0, and by Colombia in their quarter-final, despite the South American side failing to qualify for the previous tournament.

The level of competition was growing and it was evident even more so across Europe with England failing to qualify for the 2024 Olympic Games on behalf of Team GB after finishing second to the Netherlands in their Nations League group.
A draw with Portugal and defeat by Belgium were suffered by England the following year, while they were forced to overcome two penalty shootouts in Euro 2025.
There is no denying that England's competition has improved but they were still dealt a rough hand in this year's World Cup qualifying campaign.
Following their costly 4-0 defeat by Spain in June, Wiegman said: "The competition in Europe is really high.
"What I'm disappointed about is that we win five games, we have 15 points and we're in a group with the world champions and then you can't qualify.
"I'm happy with the performances but not the result of us having to go into the play-offs. That's just the way it is."

What is frustrating for England is that while they picked up a routine win over Greece and now prepare to face an opponent they have already played twice in 2026, their potential World Cup rivals are getting to play matches against top-tier teams.

Two of the tournament favourites Germany and Japan met in a friendly match on Tuesday night; Brazil and Argentina played out a 2-2 draw and four-time world champions USA played Spain twice in five days in a mouth-watering meeting.
Fifa has announced that the 2031 Women's World Cup will be expanded from 32 to 48 teams and it is too early to know if that is the right decision.
But while larger scorelines remain, it is clear it is more a direct result of a European qualification process that doesn't benefit the majority.

Later, Trump will continue his midterm campaigning blitz in Kalispell, Montana, where he’ll hold another rally.

Oral arguments are scheduled at the US Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit. The hearing comes months after the court paused a lower court’s ruling that the deployment was illegal.

Donald Trump deployed the guard in August 2025 as part of what he said was a crime-fighting mission in Washington DC. The force, which rose to a peak of about 5,000 troops over the summer, has supported arrest operations, patrolled city streets and neighborhoods and participated in cleanup efforts.
Trump’s Republican administration says the deployment has contributed to a decrease in crime in the city, where crime was already on the decline before the National Guard arrived.
Officials and activists in the overwhelmingly Democratic city say the deployment is a waste of taxpayer money and has normalized the militarization of a major American city.

“We all understand, and share, the need to contain energy prices that are weighing on families and businesses, including in Italy.

articles.headline: GTA 6 was delayed partially because the amount of NPCs was 'horrifying' and required a dedicated studio full of writers to handle
keyFacts: Grand Theft Auto 6 was delayed from May to November due to the massive scale of the game's non-player characters.
Development co-head Rob Nelson said the required projections for non-player characters were horrifying.
Rockstar established a dedicated studio in Los Angeles solely to handle the writing workload for non-player characters.
body: Grand Theft Auto 6, originally slated to be released back in May, was delayed to November—the reason given at the time was "to finish the game with the level of polish you have come to expect and deserve". And while that still very much holds true, the reality of the game's scope and stature was apparently kinda terrifying from a production standpoint.

Speaking with Bloomberg, co-head of development Rob Nelson commented on one reason for the delay—the amount of NPCs that were required to populate Leonida: "The projections they were giving us were horrifying." The solution? A kind of NPC emergency room, an entire studio set up in LA solely designed to handle the workload.

Another development co-head, Phil Hooker, comments: "I think when it became apparent that some areas weren’t going to make it, that’s when we decided to make the shift of date. We could hit that schedule, but it won’t be the game we want to make."

Being perfectly candid, for a moment: This fills me both with a sense of dread and relief. The former is acquired from the same residual existential fear I felt back in May of last year. Namely, the fact that videogames probably aren't meant to look this pretty or be this sprawling—that the industry simply cannot support them, and that GTA 6 is going to be the last of its kind.

The relief comes from the fact that, in an industry culture seemingly determined to figure out how to push creatives out of their seats as quickly as possible with AI? That a bunch of actual writers and producers were brought in to handle the load. There's this perception that background details in video games can be automated because, well, they're background details—they're not important, surely?

But in my humble opinion, those are, in fact, the details you want to get right. The background chatter and worldbuilding of a game is important because it'll lend said game its texture, even if you're just parodying Florida.

GTA 6 will be a better game because, when its developers panicked, Rockstar (which doesn't have the brightest industry track record, let's be clear) didn't cheap out on the massive writing load it'd accidentally saddled itself with, and that's commendable in a vacuum.
Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

Now, is it healthy or normal that an industry giant can be so large it can pop-up an entire studio in LA full of writers just to handle a temporary task? Probably not, and it's certainly not something that's gonna last, particularly not at the industry's current price-point.

Harvey's history with games started when he first begged his parents for a World of Warcraft subscription aged 12, though he's since been cursed with Final Fantasy 14-brain and a huge crush on G'raha Tia. He made his start as a freelancer, writing for websites like Techradar, The Escapist, Dicebreaker, The Gamer, Into the Spine—and of course, PC Gamer. He'll sink his teeth into anything that looks interesting, though he has a soft spot for RPGs, soulslikes, roguelikes, deckbuilders, MMOs, and weird indie titles. He also plays a shelf load of TTRPGs in his offline time. Don't ask him what his favourite system is, he has too many.
