articles.headline: Houthis launch new attack on Saudi capital as Trump mulls strikes
keyFacts: A Saudi military spokesman said a ballistic missile launched by the Houthis was intercepted over Riyadh, while explosions were reported in the capital.
The Houthi rebels vowed to continue targeting Saudi Arabia's international airport and oil infrastructure in response to Saudi aggression against Yemen.
President Trump stated he is considering joining attacks on the Houthis as the rebels continue targeting Saudi Arabia and threatening global energy supplies.
body: What to know about the Iran war today:

- Explosions were heard over Saudi Arabia's capital Wednesday morning between Saudi-backed forces in Yemen and . A Saudi military spokesman said a ballistic missile launched by the Houthis was intercepted over Rihadh.
- The Houthis vowed Wednesday to continue targeting Saudi Arabia's international airport and oil infrastructure in the coming days in response to "Saudi aggression" against Yemen's capital Sanaa.

- President Trump has said he's considering joining attacks on the Houthis as the rebels attack Saudi Arabia and threaten global energy supplies. The Houthis have threatened to target U.S. personnel and interests across the Middle East if Mr. Trump does order strikes, which into the sparked by the joint U.S.-Israeli strikes on Iran seven and a half months ago.
Lebanese, Iranian foreign leaders discuss situation in the Middle East
Lebanese President Joseph Aoun received a call from Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi on Wednesday to discuss the situation in the Middle East, according to the Lebanese president's office.

Both sides "discussed the current situation in the region in light of recent developments and agreed on the necessity of supporting diplomatic solutions as the best means to put an end to the conflicts in the region," the Lebanese presidency said in a statement about the call.

The Iran-backed Hezbollah militant group has been waging war with Israel in the southern part of Lebanon for months, with the official Lebanese government attempting to cool the conflict down with ceasefire agreements. Those have all been dismissed and ignored by Hezbollah.

Meanwhile, Iranian Deputy Foreign Minister Saeed Khatibzadeh arrived in Lebanon for talks with several groups. He was greeted by Lebanese Parliament Speaker Nabih Berri, who is pro-Hezbollah, and other Hezbollah representatives, according to the official Iranian news outlet IRNA.
The meeting comes amid an increase in attacks by another Iran-backed proxy group, the Yemen-based Houthis.

"During his visit, Khatibzadeh is scheduled to hold a series of meetings with senior Lebanese officials and prominent figures to discuss bilateral relations and explore opportunities to broaden cooperation between the two countries," according to IRNA.
2 more ships attacked in Hormuz: U.K. navy reports
Two ships sustained minor damage after coming under attack in the Strait of Hormuz, a British maritime agency reported Wednesday.
Both vessels were struck on Tuesday by an "unknown projectile," bringing to four the number of attacks on ships in Hormuz that day.
Iran and the United States continue to vie for control of the waterway, a vital shipping route for Gulf energy exports.
Tehran regularly targets ships it accuses of transiting without its permission, while Washington has imposed a naval blockade on Iranian ports.
The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations Centre said a 50,000-ton container ship and another 19,000-ton vessel were struck but continued on their way after sustaining only minor damage.
No casualties were reported in the attacks.

British security firm Vanguard also said attacks had targeted four ships. It identified the vessels as the GFS Pride and GFS Giselle, both sailing under Singaporean flags, and the Alfonso, which was flying a Barbados flag. The fourth ship was identified as the Al Saadiyat, sailing under the Marshall Islands flag.
According to Vanguard, , while the fate of the Alfonso, a tanker, remains unknown.
Iran says cargo ship sinks after hitting naval mine in Strait of Hormuz

Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said Wednesday that a cargo ship had sunk after hitting a naval mine in the Strait of Hormuz. It is the first time Iran has reported a ship sinking after hitting a mine during the war.

There were few details, including about the fate of the crew. Iranian state TV quoted a statement from the IRGC saying the ship was traveling on what Iran considers an illegal and dangerous route - likely the shipping lanes the U.S. has urged vessels to use, close to Oman's coast - when it hit the mine Wednesday morning.
It said the ship was carrying 2,500 containers when it first caught fire. Iran has repeatedly warned ships against trying to transit the strait without its approval.
At the end of August, President Trump declared the strait free of sea mines, saying U.S. forces had "totally cleared the strait of mines … Any boat goes through with a mine, we take it out."
There was no immediate verification of the sinking and no report by the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations monitor.
CBS/AP
Houthis warn attacks on Saudi airports, oil infrastructure will continue
The Iran-backed Houthi rebels in Yemen said Wednesday that they would continue targeting Saudi Arabia's international airport and oil infrastructure in the coming days

In a televised statement, Houthi military spokesman Brig. Gen. Yahya Saree said the attacks were "in response to the treacherous Saudi aggression against the capital Sanaa and the free governorates" and part of the group's "deterrence operations against the Saudi aggressor."

Saree also warned international shipping companies, civilians, and employees working at the targeted airports and businesses to "stay away from them and evacuate them immediately," as they would be considered legitimate targets.
Saudis say another Houthi ballistic missile targeting Riyadh was intercepted
A spokesperson for the Saudi-led coalition forces said Wednesday they had intercepted an attack from the Iran-backed Houthi militia.
Coalition spokesman Turki al-Maliki said in a post on X a ballistic missile "launched by the terrorist Houthi militia towards Riyadh has been intercepted and destroyed."
Earlier, residents in the Saudi capital had reported hearing explosions.
Residents in Saudi Arabia's capital say they have heard new explosions in Riyadh
Residents in Saudi Arabia's capital say they have heard new explosions in Riyadh.
The residents spoke on condition of anonymity for their safety. One lives in northern Riyadh, where King Khalid International Airport is located.

The source of the explosions wasn't immediately clear. The Saudi civil defense reported air raid alerts in Riyadh and Kharj province southeast of the capital. Kharj is home to the state-owned Military Industries Corporation and Prince Sultan Air Base.
The airport in Riyadh has been targeted several times in the past week with deadly attacks. Iran-backed Houthi rebels in neighboring Yemen have claimed responsibility.
Intercepted missiles over Riyadh injure at least 4 people, officials say
Saudi Arabia's Civil Defense said debris from two intercepted Houthi missiles fell on residential areas in Riyadh on Tuesday, injuring four people and damaging 15 homes.
State-run Saudi Press Agency reported the injured included two women, a man and a child. Images released by Saudi's Civil Defense showed broken windows caused by what it said was fallen shrapnel.
CBS/AP
Building fire reported in Aramco compound targeted by Houthis, Saudi officials say

The Saudi Ministry of Energy said Tuesday a limited fire broke out in an administrative building in Aramco, one of the world's largest oil facilities, that was targeted in the country's Eastern Province. The ministry said no injuries were reported.

The attack comes as the Iranian-backed Houthis and the Saudi coalition exchanged attacks Tuesday night. It marks a fresh escalation in the widening Middle East crisis and came shortly after the Saudi coalition reported a series of alerts for incoming missiles heading for the country's Eastern Province, a major oil-producing region and the capital Riyadh.
Saudi-led forces confirm strikes on Yemen oil sites

The Saudi-led coalition battling the Iran-backed Houthis confirmed it struck oil sites across western Yemen on Tuesday, including in the capital Sanaa, in response to the deadliest attack on the kingdom's soil in years.
Blasts were heard shortly after in Saudi capital Riyadh and at an oil giant Aramco facility in eastern Saudi Arabia, witnesses and journalists told AFP.

Tuesday's coalition strikes in Yemen's Sanaa and the western provinces of Dhamar and Saada targeted facilities used to "supply the war effort" by the Houthis to "threaten the kingdom, Yemen, the southern Red Sea and waterways," coalition spokesman Turki al-Maliki wrote on X.
An AFP correspondent in Sanaa reported an explosion, while a breaking news alert on the Houthi-affiliated Al-Masirah TV channel said earlier that "Saudi aggression" targeted the oil firm.

articles.headline: I Put the Oppo Find X10 Pro’s Camera to the Test. These Are the Results
keyFacts: CNET tested the unreleased Oppo Find X10 Pro flagship Android phone in Edinburgh ahead of its official unveiling.
The reviewer stated they are currently barred by a non-disclosure agreement from discussing specific camera hardware specifications.
A full review and camera details will be published later in the month.
body: Oppo’s latest flagship Android phone, the Find X10 Pro is set to be unveiled in the coming weeks, but Oppo kindly sent me a unit ahead of time to let me take its cameras for a spin. So I did. I’ve been on multiple walks around my home in sunny Edinburgh and have taken a variety of snaps with the phone’s multiple rear cameras.

The fun part here is that while I can show you the photos — and you can see the phone in my hand above — I’m not yet allowed to talk about any specs, including the resolution of the cameras or what technology is powering them. So instead, I’m presenting these photos just as they are, almost as a little teaser ahead of the phone’s full unveiling later in the month. I’ll have a full review ready then, along with all the information about the cameras and some comparisons against other top Android camera phones like the Leica Leitzphone.

But all of that’s to come. For now, enjoy some of my early test images taken with the X10 Pro, along with as much information as my non-disclosure agreement allows me to share. Keep in mind that all photos have been imported into Adobe Lightroom in order to be easily assessed and resized for publishing online. No other edits, including sharpening, have been applied unless otherwise stated.
More from CNET
Taken with the main camera, this image is sharp, packed with detail and has natural colors.

I don’t think I’m breaking any rules in telling you that the phone has an ultrawide camera, so here’s a photo I took with it. It looks a little more drab than the one from the main camera, but it’s still got plenty of detail.

There are various color filters, which I almost certainly can’t tell you about here, but you probably assumed it had them anyway, right? Right?! Anyway, I used one of them (I won’t say which) to take this shot, and I like the filmic vibes it’s produced.
I used a different, unnamed, color filter here and I like the punchy tones, especially from that flash of red at the bottom of the ship.
While this color filter is much more subtle, it gives a bold blue that contrasts nicely with the building’s orange.

The last two generations of Oppo phones (including the superb Find X9 Ultra) had Hasselblad’s XPan mode, so I can’t imagine it’s a secret that the new one does too. This mode allows you to shoot with a wide, narrow crop that’s reminiscent of Hasselblad’s legendary XPan panoramic film camera. Those cameras are rare and expensive, so this is the closest you’ll probably get to an authentic XPan experience. I love this wide, cinematic aspect ratio.

While I love the vibrancy of this image — and the sense of the warm evening glow — I do think the camera’s image processing has gone a bit hard with the “HDR” here, creating a less realistic-looking shot.

That over-processing is especially noticeable here. It’s as though the phone has desperately tried to eliminate any shadow in the image, creating a flat-looking shot that lacks the rich tones you’d expect from a good camera.

The Find X10 Pro isn’t alone in this regard — I find most phones seem to go too hard on image processing, and that includes the Find X9 Ultra. The way around it is to shoot in Master mode, taking control of your white balance settings and shooting in DNG raw to avoid any built-in software and AI-based processing being applied. I made my own tweaks to this image in Adobe Lightroom.
While this shot is a straight-out-of-camera image taken in the default mode. Again, I’d have to say that it looks over-processed, especially with the artificially brightened shadows.

I took this shot in Master Mode specifically so I could take control of the white balance and warm the scene up to emphasise that glorious morning sunshine. I took it in JPEG and have done no further editing.
Yes, the phone has a telephoto zoom lens, but no I can’t tell you what that zoom factor is. What I can say is that I think this shot looks good.
And this telephoto zoom shot also looks good, with sharp details and vibrant colors.

Like the Find X9 Ultra, the X10 Pro will be available with an add-on telephoto zoom lens to take your zoom shots even further. Here’s a white pigeon I found. While the camera struggled to get focus on the bird (getting confused by the railing in front) it eventually achieved an impressively sharp image, with natural-looking bokeh from the out-of-focus railing.

And another with the add-on telephoto lens. This time it’s a seagull on a boat, even though it doesn’t need a boat because it can fly. This seagull just wants to have everything and it’s a real shame that late-stage capitalism has influenced the local birdlife in this way.

Speaking of capitalism, I’ll end on this photo of yours truly with a Leica M6 slung around my neck. Taken with the front-facing camera, this shot has nice-looking tones, both in terms of the shadows and the colors.

I like many of these early test shots I’ve taken, and I’m looking forward to spending more time with the phone over the coming weeks. It has some stiff competition – not just from the aforementioned Leica Leitzphone and the new iPhone 18 Pro, but also from its predecessor, the Find X9 Ultra, which impressed me with its photography skills when I reviewed it in June.

articles.headline: Fernando Mendoza tipped for ‘outstanding’ career as ex-NFL star recalls emotional first
keyFacts: Former NFL player Jason Bell told talkSPORT that he wants to collect rookie trading cards for Las Vegas Raiders quarterback Fernando Mendoza.
Bell said he predicts an outstanding career for Mendoza, who made his NFL debut during a Week 5 loss to the New England Patriots.
Bell also stated he is hunting for rookie cards of defensive players Caleb Downs, Sonny Styles, and Arvell Reese.
body: There’s nothing like knowing that you’ve achieved your dream to play in the NFL than seeing your face on your first trading card.
But for avid card collectors, including former NFL cornerback and safety Jason Bell, there’s no greater feeling than picking up rookie cards of the next generation of stars.
Former NFL star Bell revealed to talkSPORT that he is hunting down Fernando Mendoza’s rookie card to add to his collection Topps Fanatics

As the NFL continues its three-week stint in London, the former Dallas Cowboys , Houston Texans , and New York Giants defender was present at Fanatics Collectibles’ flagship store in Regent Street , London, where he discussed his love for Topps trading cards.
With the latest rookie class having now entered the league, Bell spoke exclusively to talkSPORT on whose cards he is on the hunt for this season to add to his lucrative collection.

There was no surprise that No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza is high up on the 48-year-old’s want list, with the Las Vegas Raiders quarterback entering the league with a huge amount of hype around him.

“This season, even watching Fernando Mendoza play the other day, I would absolutely love to pull his card. I think he’s going to have an outstanding career, and I love the kind of player he is,” Bell told talkSPORT.
View this post on Instagram

Mendoza has begun his rookie campaign learning the game behind veteran signal caller Kirk Cousins , but took to the field to make his debut in the Raiders’ Week 5 45-17 blowout loss to the New England Patriots .
Seeing some on-field action – albeit limited – in the fourth quarter, the former Indiana Hoosiers star completed six of his eight passing attempts for 48 yards.
But the Heisman Trophy winner isn’t the only player who Bell is looking to pull from a pack this season.
“I’d also love Caleb Downs,” Bell continued. “I think, as a safety, what he does is fantastic. I loved him as a player coming out. Sonny Styles, I’d love, and Arvell Reese, too.
“These are a few defenders who I think are going to have substantial careers, so I’d love to have their cards in my collection. That would be really cool.”

Despite the Cowboys’ poor start to the season, especially on the defensive side of the ball, former Alabama and Ohio State safety has been one of the bright sparks , having already recorded 31 tackles (19 solo), a QB hit, a sack and two forced fumbles.
Mendoza made his official NFL debut in Week 5, coming in for some late fourth-quarter action Getty
Commanders safety Sonny Styles has been a particular rookie standout so far this season Getty

Similarly, Reese has been instrumental to a Giants defense that has the G-Men off to a 3-1-1 start to the 2026 campaign, having already racked up 43 tackles (30 solo), four tackles for loss, two QB hits, one sack, and one interception.
So far, every Buckeye that was an early draft pick in 2026 appears to have turned into gold, with Styles also proving he was worthy of being the seventh overall pick to the Washington Commanders .

In his first five games of his professional career, the 21-year-old linebacker has 33 tackles (15 solo), three tackles for loss, two QB hits, a forced fumble, a sack, and an interception on a Commanders team that ranks 30th in the NFL in points allowed (29.8 PPG).
What it means to be on an NFL trading card
Making it to the NFL as an undrafted free agent out of UCLA, Bell, unlike the drafted rookies, had to bide his time before seeing himself on a trading card for the very first time.
But it was worth the wait, and served as a small token of acknowledgement that all the hard work had paid off and he had achieved his dream to play in the NFL.

“It took a while because I wasn’t drafted, so I didn’t immediately have a card. But after I’d been in the league for a while, I finally saw one, and it was one of those moments where it flashed back to being a kid and thinking, ‘Oh my gosh, I’m here,'” Bell told talkSPORT.
Bell recalls how he felt when he saw himself on a trading card for the very first time Topps Fanatics

“I’d already been playing for a couple of years, but it kind of didn’t even feel real until I got that card. You’re just like, ‘Oh no, it’s official. I’m here.’ It’s a level of representation that says you’ve earned your right to be in the league.
“And now some kid somewhere who’s never heard of me, who doesn’t know who I am, opens up that card and goes, ‘Wow, Jason Bell.’
“It just made me very thankful and appreciative of what it took to get there,” he added. “Now I’m part of the NFL and the landscape of it all.

“Because of those cards, that physical thing feels like you’ve made it. It just made me feel proud to be part of the NFL and something I really love and care about, having grown up doing the same thing.”
The 2026 Topps Flagship Football London Store Exclusive Mega Box is available exclusively at the Fanatics Collectibles London Flagship Store on Regent Street.

articles.headline: GTA 6 leaker's latest video allegedly shows scenes from the final mission, as they indicate the leaks may have come to an end
keyFacts: Grand Theft Auto 6 leaker Cyberleek released a new video allegedly showing parts of the game's final mission.
Cyberleek indicated they are stopping leaks because their cryptocurrency promotion failed to reach its targeted market capitalization.
Cyberleek's cryptocurrency market cap dropped to $1.2m, and the leaker stated the leaks stop for now.
body: Cyberleek, the leaker who's been releasing footage from Grand Theft Auto 6 for weeks now, is seemingly done posting leaks. Cyberleek released a new - seemingly final - video today which supposedly shows parts of the game's ending.

The leaker has indicated they may be done sharing footage as their goal of pumping their crypto coin had failed. Cyberleek recently said they'd release a 200GB build of the game if the coin hits $30m market cap, which it's nowhere near doing.

The coin has crashed in recent weeks after a major bump that coincided with the release of leaked footage showing co-protagonist Lucia fully naked, shortly after they released footage of co-protagonist Jason also nude.

Eurogamer has seen the latest footage, and it's not as dramatic as Cyberleek initially made it out to be. The footage does not appear to be of the game's ending sequence or final cutscene, though the location of where the action takes place could be a spoiler. The four-minute video ends with a montage of various locations and flyover footage of a city, set to Journey's Don't Stop Believin'.
There may be something there, but when viewed without proper context, it's hard to say what's actually being spoiled. Still, the footage is best avoided if you want to jump into the game fresh.

"The 30m was not reached, so no build," Cyberleek reportedly said in a message posted on their website. "Uploading 200+ GB anonymously is a serious risk - worth it only if the milestone funded the secret project."

At the time of writing, Cyberleek's memecoin's market cap has dropped to $1.2m just three days after reaching its peak of $7.8m. It also seems they've abandoned the initial plan to tie certain gameplay leaks to the coin's market cap.

"The leeks stop here. For now," Cyberleek allegedly wrote, though it's worth keeping in mind that the leaker reappeared last week after going to ground following their initial leaks in August, seemingly in response to Rockstar parent company Take-Two initiating a massive investigation and issuing subpoenas to Discord and Microsoft.
Given recent history, Cyberleek could simply re-emerge yet again with a new scam and more footage. GTA 6's 19th November official launch is not far off, however, so their window is closing.

articles.headline: November Supplemental Security direct payment up to $994 goes out in 16 days
keyFacts: November 2026 Supplemental Security Income payments worth up to $994 will be sent to recipients in 16 days.
Because Nov. 1 falls on a Sunday, recipients will receive their benefits early on Friday, Oct. 30.
The program supports individuals with limited income who are blind, age 65 or older, or have a qualifying disability.
body: The November 2026 Supplemental Security Income payments, worth up to $994 for an individual filer, will be sent to recipients in 16 days.

SSI payments are typically issued on the first day of each month, or on the last business day of the prior month if the first day falls on a federal holiday. Nov. 1 is a Sunday, so recipients will receive their benefits on Friday, Oct. 30.
The program supports people with limited income who are blind, age 65 or older, or have another qualifying disability.

The amount beneficiaries receive varies based on several factors, including the number of people filing and the individual’s income. Typically, the more income the filer has, whether earned or unearned, the lower their payments would be. Individual filers can receive up to $994, couples filing jointly can receive $1,491, and those providing essential care to SSI recipients can receive up to $498.

Filers must meet certain requirements and prerequisites for receiving SSI payments . Recipients must also be U.S. citizens or noncitizens in one of the alien classifications granted by the Department of Homeland Security. Senior citizens at retirement age (65) typically receive lower payments because they also receive Social Security benefits.

Recipients must also live in one of the 50 states, the District of Columbia, or the Northern Mariana Islands, and must not be absent from the United States for a full calendar month or 30 consecutive days. SSI is not available in American Samoa, Guam, Puerto Rico, and the U.S. Virgin Islands.
A full calendar for the Social Security Administration payments can be viewed on the agency’s website.

articles.headline: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake plays even better than it looks
keyFacts: Nintendo is releasing a remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time for the Switch 2.
The preview showed updated visuals, new gameplay buttons for jumping and sprinting, and full voice acting for cutscenes.
The game is available for pre-order now for sixty dollars ahead of its official release on November 5.
body: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake plays even better than it looks
Link is getting a lot more than just a visual glow up for the new Switch 2 version.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is simply one of the best video games ever. Not only did it redefine a beloved franchise after it made the jump from 2D to 3D following A Link to the Past, it sits alone at the top of Metacritic's all-time rankings, a full point higher than other legendary titles like Soulcalibur, GTA IV and Super Mario Galaxy 2. When Nintendo announced that it was remaking the classic title from 1998, the hype was more than understandable. And now that I've had a chance to play a preview of this new version for the Switch 2, I can safely say that it plays even better than it looks.

It's easy to focus a ton on the game's updated visuals. While the original looked great for a 3D title back in the late 90s when most games were still confined to two dimensions, the N64 had its limits, and more than 20 years later, the game is showing its age. But with this remake, Nintendo has completely reshaped Hyrule and given it a loving makeover befitting a new release in 2026.

With its fresh graphical treatment, everything just feels so full of life. Kokiri Forest is lush and overgrown, while the main square in Hyrule Castle Town is bustling with people and pets. Taller buildings and new alleys add a sense of depth and dimension you didn't really get from the original. But I'd argue that things get even better when you focus on smaller details, like the textures on various items. The wise old owl, Kaepora Gaebora, now appears wonderfully fluffy yet still distinguished, while objects like the Deku Shield fit in even better with its surroundings. Instead of looking like a thick piece of cardboard with a swirl on it, you can actually see the bark it's made out of and how it's just as much a piece of the forest as the rest of the village. Meanwhile, Link's nose finally has a more natural shape, instead of looking like it's sharp enough to cut glass.

Things get even better when you go exploring. Inside the Forest Temple, there are rooms with low lying fog that swirls around as you search for items, which enhances the spooky atmosphere. However, my favorite touch is the new effects you see when Link swings his sword. There are brilliant particles that burst out when you make contact with an enemy while the updated animation for his Spin Attack sends out waves of energy, adding even more emphasis to our hero's signature move.

My one small gripe with the remake's updated graphics is that water doesn't look quite right. For example, after going for a swim, it almost looks like Link is covered in high-fructose corn syrup instead of water. When you check out various streams and rivers, they seem to be filled with light blue jello instead of good 'ole H20. But the appearance of water is something that a lot of modern games still have trouble with and it's easy enough to overlook considering how good the rest of the game's visuals are.

As for gameplay, Nintendo smartly decided not to mess too much with the original's formula. You still rely a lot on Z-targeting (locking onto nearby enemies by pressing one of the Z shoulder buttons), which feels kind of quaint nowadays. However, there is now an actual jump button for navigating platforms and obstacles, which makes running around feel a lot more natural. There's also a new sprint button for quickly getting around. That said, if you want to pretend it's 1998 and roll everywhere, you can do that too, and like the rest of the game's movement, running, fighting and traversing the world feels a lot smoother and less clunky than it did back in the day.

Nintendo also added cutscenes with full voice acting, which adds an extra level of gravitas to things like meeting the Great Deku tree for the first time. And just like before, you still have Navi yelling "Hey, Listen!" at you, which even though it might get annoying after a while, I wouldn't have it any other way. The one small downside to this is that when you're just running around town and talking to lower-level NPCs, dialogue is still mostly text-based, which can make Link's limited speaking abilities feel like something is missing sometimes.

Some other new quality of life features includes the Threads of Time system which adds helpful story summaries and tool tips so it's easier to remember what you were doing in the game and pick up where you left off. You also now have full control over camera positioning in case you get stuck in an awkward position, though I found that I didn't need it very often. Swimming has also been improved a ton and the inventory screen has been reworked too, so swapping between tools and weapons is even faster than before. These are just some of the more obvious upgrades; there are a ton of little or more subtle changes like Link actually pushing on things to open doors, full day/night cycles, tweaks to the game's map and landscape and others. Heck, you can even hum or sing into the Switch 2 to play notes on the in-game ocarina if traditional button inputs aren't your thing. And when you hear tunes like the Song of Time again, it hits hard.

There's just so much going on in the Ocarina of Time remake, even for people like me who played it when it first came out almost thirty years ago. The game still feels fresh and exciting while retaining everything that made it the classic it is today. This means that regardless of whether you're a long-time fan or someone new to the franchise, there's a lot to like and I can't wait to explore how deep all of Nintendo's changes go this time around.
The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time for the Switch 2 is available for pre-order now for $60, ahead of its official release on November 5.

articles.headline: Anthropic warns small AI models could self-replicate through IoT devices
keyFacts: AI company Anthropic warned that small AI models could soon enable self-replicating malware capable of infecting various Internet-of-things devices.
Anthropic stated that such a replicator would be challenging to shut down because it lacks a centralized point of failure and adapts to unfamiliar devices.
Company researchers successfully ran small open-weight models on low-cost hardware during a recent experiment.
body: AI company Anthropic is warning that advances in small AI models could soon usher in a new era of self-replicating malware that’s capable of infecting smart fridges, vacuum cleaners, and a wide range of other Internet-of-things devices and is more resistant to takedown.

By next year, smaller AI models may be able to autonomously self-replicate on all kinds of IoT devices, the company said. Eventually, the capability could enable computer worms, which propagate without requiring human interaction and are capable of infecting unfamiliar IoT devices. An experiment the company performed recently revealed significant challenges in bringing such an AI malware replicator to fruition, so the finding is necessarily tempered. Still, the results do raise concerns about the possibility of new forms of computer worms.
Challenging to shut down

Anthropic further warned not only about the new potential malware, but also that it could be difficult to stop. In its blog post, it wrote that “a replicator like this would be challenging to shut down, since there’s no centralized point to shut off—though it may be slow (with a doubling time of days). Unlike non-AI malware, it could also figure out unfamiliar devices on its own.”

Smaller AI models require much less powerful hardware to run than do frontier models. Anthropic ran small open-weight models on real or simulated low-cost, off-brand Android TV boxes and other types of IoT hardware. Company researchers found that by using quantization to represent the models using fewer bits and splitting the workloads into “shards” running on each device, the models were able to establish inference, meaning that the model weights loaded and could generate output.

The lightweight Gemma4-26B-A4B model required just 15 boxes, each equipped with only 4GB of memory, to achieve inference. The Qwen3.5-9B was able to configure other LLMs to run on eight of nine hardware types. Unlike traditional malware, which must be written to run on specific hardware or software, the model was able to use its weights to make configurations on the fly that were specific to the devices it was tested against.

articles.headline: GTA 6 Leaker Releases New Gameplay Video Showing Snippets of the Final Missions, Declares 'The End of the Road' After Crypto Scheme Collapses
keyFacts: The person or group known as Cyberleek allegedly released a new unauthorized GTA 6 gameplay video showing parts of the story's ending.
Cyberleek declared the end of the leaks because their memecoin failed to reach the required $30 million market cap target.
Cyberleek claimed they will not release an alleged 200GB build of the game, but warned they have a dead man's switch for story spoilers.
body: The GTA 6 leaker has allegedly released a new unauthorized gameplay video which reportedly shows parts of the ending of the story, sparking significant spoiler concern among fans online. IGN will not report on the details of the leaked video.

Meanwhile, Cyberleek — the person or group responsible for the high-profile GTA 6 leaks that began in the summer — has suggested they will now stop leaking the game. They also claim they will not risk releasing an alleged 200GB build of GTA 6 because their memecoin failed to hit the $30 million market cap target that had been set for its release.

However, Cyberleek claims to have a "dead man's switch" for story spoilers, which they have reportedly threatened to flip if they are threatened, presumably by either Rockstar Games or parent company Take-Two.

Yesterday, we reported on how GTA 6 fans were celebrating the crash of the Cyberleek memecoin after the leaker had tied various types of gameplay leaks to its market cap, ranging from $5 million to $25 million. The leaker also threatened to release a build of the game — supposedly over 200GB in size — if the memecoin hit a $30 million market cap.

Earlier this week, a number of gameplay clips were reportedly leaked after market cap goals were hit, including gameplay that allegedly shows Lucia fully naked, and, more recently, the alleged leak of a “Lucia closeup 4k” video.

Cyberleek then threatened to release a new unauthorized GTA 6 gameplay video every day, assuming the memecoin market cap targets were met, and launched yet another gameplay poll designed to encourage spending on the memecoin.

However, the Cyberleek memecoin crashed, with a current market cap of $1.2 million, down from a high of $7.8 million on October 11. With those targets now pretty much impossible, it sounds like Cyberleek's crypto scheme has come to an end.

In a new message reportedly posted to their website, Cyberleek declared "the end of the road." In the post, Cyberleek defended their actions from crypto scam allegations, and said Take-Two was "punished enough." "The ending stays unpublished," Cyberleek allegedly insisted in the message. They claimed that while the latest leak does show clips from the final missions of the game, out of context they do not spoil the story.
It's fair to say many fans have taken issue with that suggestion, and are already taking steps to avoid spoilers online.

Cyberleek's message also suggests that the build of GTA 6 they allegedly have access to will not be released because the $30 million market cap was not reached. Cyberleek had said they were raising funds for some mystery project, although many didn't believe the claim. "Uploading 200+ GB anonymously is a serious risk," they said, "worth it only if the milestone funded the secret project." They said the memecoin should have been considered a "donation," not an "investment," and hit out at "influencers" who claimed otherwise.
Then, the upshot: "The leeks stop here. For now."

Of course, Cyberleek may release further gameplay and continue with their crypto scheme anyway. They may even release the build they allegedly have. For now though, the more pressing concern is avoiding spoilers sparked by today's leaked video.

Fans had spent the last week calling on people not to spend money on Cyberleek, pointing out the leaker cashed out back in August and is likely to do so again ahead of GTA 6’s official release date, if they haven’t already. Analysis of cryptocurrency transactions in late August pointed to the GTA 6 leaker cashing out having earnt around $270,000.

Earlier this week, IGN reported on fan skepticism around the alleged leaked gameplay that reportedly showed both Jason and Lucia fully naked. A previous leaked gameplay video allegedly showed a tank spawning into the world, which suggests access to a dev menu of some kind. The leaked videos allegedly showing both Jason and Lucia fully naked also show NPCs failing to react to nudity in any way, which suggests this effect was achieved with either a dev menu or cheats and won’t be possible in the official release.

One theory is that Cyberleak was able to access this state for both Lucia and Jason because in at least one mission players will see both characters naked, perhaps in a nudist resort. As it stands, this is all speculation, and it is unknown if GTA 6 will feature either character naked at any point — officially at least.

Cyberleek appeared to go dark after a spate of high-profile GTA 6 leaks in August that sparked an investigation from Take-Two. The company issued subpoenas to the likes of Discord as part of the hunt for the person or group of people responsible. But Cyberleek reemerged last week with the release of a 24-minute GTA 6 gameplay video that reportedly showed cutscenes, story beats, playable characters Jason and Lucia naked (in the case of Jason, full-frontal nudity), and a first-person camera.

It remains unclear how the gameplay footage, or any potential build of the game it's taken from, escaped the confines of Rockstar's infamous tight security. Recent developments suggest Cyberleek remains at large and defiant in the face of potential legal action.

In August, Rockstar addressed the GTA 6 leaks, describing the situation as "heartbreaking" for its development team and "unfortunate" for fans. At the time, the developer acknowledged that its intended experience for players "may now be impacted by some spoilers," but reiterated GTA 6's previously-confirmed launch date of November 19.

Whether the culprit or culprits are ever caught may rest on how successful Take-Two's legal team and the relevant authorities are at forcing social networks or crypto exchanges to divulge any personal details they hold on those responsible.

articles.headline: Trump’s bizarre new transit plan could hurt the families who need it most
keyFacts: The Trump administration announced a transit plan tying federal public transit funding to high fertility and marriage rates.
Communities with high numbers of traditional nuclear families could receive a 10 percent funding boost for transit projects under the plan.
Critics argue the policy will benefit wealthier suburban areas while potentially harming urban families who rely on public transit.
body: The Trump administration’s transit policies won’t “make travel family-friendly again” in the ways that matter most. | GraphicaArtis/Getty Images
“We should look for love!” Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy bellowed while flanked by his nine children at the Great American State Fair in June: “Get married, and have lots of kids!”

In a brazen attempt to make Duffy’s ethos a matter of policy, the Trump administration announced a strange new plan earlier this month tying a huge tranche of federal funding for public transit to high fertility and marriage rates .

If the plan goes into effect, then communities with a high number of traditional nuclear families could get a 10 percent funding boost to build new trains, bus routes, and ferry lines. “If you want federal funding,” Duffy’s Transportation Department said in a statement , then “your project needs to align with where communities and families are actually growing.”

Trump, who has dubbed himself the “ fertilization president ,” and his bevvy of neopatriarchal trad – pilled deputies have long nursed a fixation with the country’s declining birth rate . But dubious as this new policy may be, it stumbles upon a genuine pain point in the nation’s public transit systems: They are not nearly as family friendly as they should be. And regardless of whether these discomfitingly pronatalist guidelines ever go into effect as written — and they probably will — they raise important questions about how American families use our transit systems now, and the policies could actually make their lives easier in the long run.

The same woes that affect all riders — long wait times, inaccessible stations, inadequate reach, and crowded rush hours — often doubly affect families. That’s one reason why so many of them have fled the nation’s densest, most transit-oriented cities in search of suburbs where they need not lug a stroller up yet another broken escalator to reach a subway platform.

Families who can’t afford to trade in their MetroCards and bus passes for minivans may find themselves priced into housing served by especially substandard transit options, funneling them into brutal, hours-long commutes. According to one landmark study, the single strongest factor in predicting social mobility in the US is neither crime nor test scores nor the presence of “traditional” two-parent households, but access to adequate transportation . With every extra minute a child spends commuting to school, they become less likely to move out poverty as an adult.

And for that reason alone, American families with kids do deserve special attention when it comes to how and where and why we build public transit. On this, the Trump administration got something right, even if they got there for all the wrong reasons — ones that I, a childless woman of childbearing age, find vaguely ethnonationalist, and above all, personally creepy.

But families often need public transportation most in the places where it’s otherwise hardest to raise kids — which is to say in dense cities rather than in already car-centric suburbs. In that sense, especially, In fact, it might make circumstances even worse for the families that really rely on public transit every day.
What family-friendly public transit actually looks like

Marriage and birth rates might sound like a reasonable proxy for where families live, but in reality, according to an analysis by the Urban Institute, the places with the most “ traditional” nuclear families tend to be whiter and wealthier than the population at large, and are much more likely to get around by car, not trains or buses.

We are talking about the suburbs here, which, while certainly deserving of their own transit infrastructure, rarely rely on trains or buses the way that a carless family living on the outer edges of a major city might. And yet the Trump administration has typically treated those very communities — some of which do, in fact, have high birth rates — with contempt or even outright antipathy.

Consider Chicago’s Red Line, the busiest corridor of the city’s L rail system, which serves some 138 million people per year. The line has long been in need of expansion, and a $5.7 billion extension close to 60 years in the making finally broke ground earlier this year. It will add 5.5 more miles of track with four new stations in the city’s southernmost neighborhoods.

For over half a century, families in the far South Side of Chicago have cobbled together grueling commutes that force them to transfer from buses and trains to reach downtown Chicago, which helps explain why unemployment and poverty rates in the area remain so stubbornly high. Communities like Roseland, where many of the new stations will be built, are considered to be among the most challenging places in the nation to raise a child , but thousands of local families still find ways to do so.

Roseland has a much higher birth rate than the national average, meaning that in theory, Duffy’s transportation department should be itching to send extra funds to transit projects there. But first they have to be willing to fund it at all, and if past policies hold, they may be reluctant to do just that. Just last year, the Trump administration opted to freeze federal funds already allocated to the Red Line extension , plunging the long-awaited project into yet another prolonged period of infrastructural purgatory.

That move plays into a broader pattern: The Trump administration has hampered dozens of transit projects like the Red Line, seemingly in its broader push to starve Democratic-led cities of federal infrastructure dollars. While a federal judge eventually intervened to allow the Red Line extension to proceed , if the Trump administration’s new guidelines go into effect after public comments close in November, then more projects like it in other urban communities will likely be deprioritized.
Ultimately, it is the suburbanites who are most poised to benefit from the Trump administration’s proposed policy.

An example is FrontRunner 2X in Utah, a commuter rail project that will slash travel time for Utahns traveling across the state, and will also help Salt Lake City shoulder an influx of tourists when it hosts the Olympics in 2034 . It received federal support through the same tranche of funding as Chicago’s Red Line extension. In stark contrast with that more urban initiative, FrontRunner 2X has been the rare public transit project to receive continued support under the Trump administration.

Utah has some of the highest birth and marriage rates in the country, so it’s not a stretch of the imagination to say that if the Trump administration has its way, then the United States will see more projects like FrontRunner 2X get funded, while others like the Red Line extension face bureaucratic bottlenecks and funding freezes. Roseland’s high birth rate notwithstanding, the neighborhood has some of the lowest marriage rates in the country, meaning that even if a project there did manage to eke out federal support, then according to this new calculus, it would still receive significantly less funding from the federal government than a place like the suburbs of Salt Lake City where married families with children are more common.

Trump’s new pronatalist transit agenda is, at the very least, an indication that after two years spent twiddling their thumbs, firing Amtrak executives , and venerating cars big and small , he may finally be building a semi-coherent transit strategy. And his Transportation Department has allowed a few genuinely family-friendly upgrades for the country’s transit infrastructure to proceed, including grants to add space for strollers on trains and buses.

But you can’t claim to support American families while siphoning federal dollars away from the projects that could actually be transformational to their lives. I am not one to decry a commuter rail renaissance, but it shouldn’t come at the expense of places where American families — the ones Duffy says he’s so keen on having more babies — don’t have any other choice but to wait an hour for the bus to get to work.

articles.headline: NFL star Tyreek Hill’s estranged wife awarded $500,000 damages in battery trial
keyFacts: A Miami jury found NFL wide receiver Tyreek Hill liable for two counts of battery against his estranged wife, Lakeeta Vaccaro, awarding her $500,000 in compensatory damages.
The jury cleared Hill of eight other claims made by Vaccaro, which included additional counts of battery, assault, and continuing domestic violence.
Hill's agent indicated that Hill wishes to return to the NFL as he recovers from a knee injury suffered in September 2025.
body: A Miami jury on Tuesday found Tyreek Hill liable for two counts of battery but not liable for the eight remaining claims made by Lakeeta Vaccaro – ending the high-profile civil trial involving the NFL wide receiver and his estranged wife.

Hill, who has played for the NFL’s Kansas City Chiefs and Miami Dolphins, was found liable for two counts of battery – one stemming from an incident in January 2024, and another from April 2025. The jury awarded Vaccaro $500,000 in compensatory damages but did not award her punitive damages.
The jury found Hill, 32, not liable for eight other counts that included battery, assault and continuing domestic violence.

The trial involved allegations of abuse made by Vaccaro, 30, who on the stand described instances in which Hill allegedly pulled her hair and “treated me like I was, just, a man.” The jury was also shown a photo Vaccaro took of markings on her chest that she says were made during an argument between the pair. Hill took the stand last week and mostly denied what he called “false allegations” made by his estranged wife, while saying in one instance he shoved Vaccaro and “created a hole in the wall.”
Hill embraced one of his attorneys and shook hands with others following the verdict before leaving the courtroom by himself.
Vaccaro’s lawyer, Paul Schwiep, had asked the jury to “restore her dignity” and was seeking $8m in damages from Hill.
“Money doesn’t undo the harm, but it’s just how our civil justice system works,” Schwiep said.
Christi Bright said Hill was thankful after the trial.
“Mr Hill was very pleased that he was able to get his story out and to be able to tell the world what he’s not been able to speak about,” Bright told reporters. “He’s very grateful.”

Hill is still working his way back from a dislocated knee and torn ligaments suffered in September 2025 while he was with the Dolphins, but his agent, Drew Rosenhaus, has indicated that his client wishes to return to the NFL.

articles.headline: Trump posts wild video of him taming tiger after ex-child star mauled to death at UK zoo
keyFacts: President Trump posted an AI-generated video showing him chasing and befriending a Siberian tiger.
The post followed an earlier video shared by Trump of a tiger fatally attacking 23-year-old William Chapman at a UK zoo.
Chapman's family stated that he suffered from significant mental illness and asked authorities to investigate why he entered the enclosure.
body: President Trump posted a wild AI-generated video late Tuesday that showed him chasing, tackling and befriending a Siberian tiger, hours after he had warned his Truth Social followers: “Don’t ever mess with nature!”

The president initially posted gruesome video Tuesday afternoon of the beast fatally savaging 23-year-old William Chapman at Yorkshire Wildlife Park in Doncaster, England over the weekend, accompanied by his admonition.
About eight hours later, Trump posted the artificial clip, which began with himself on the ground in Chapman’s place.
The altered video then showed the president — in full blue suit and red tie — pursuing the big cat before playfully wrestling with it and grabbing it in a bear hug.
There was no message accompanying the AI generated video, which was posted after the president finished addressing a pre-midterm election rally in Alaska.

Chapman’s family said Tuesday their loved one suffered from “significant mental illness” and asked local authorities to figure out why their loved one jumped into the tiger enclosure shortly before his death.

articles.headline: Trump says 'we are looking into' other Dan Sullivan on Alaska ballot, warns about governor's race
keyFacts: President Donald Trump stated in an interview that federal authorities are looking into an independent challenger named Dan Sullivan running in the Alaska Senate race.
Trump claimed the second candidate named Dan Sullivan was a Democratic hoax designed to siphon votes away from the Republican incumbent, Sen. Dan Sullivan.
Trump also called on primary loser Dave Bronson to drop out of the Alaska gubernatorial race to prevent vote-splitting against the Democratic candidate.
body: President Donald Trump says federal authorities are "looking into" Dan Sullivan, an independent challenger who goes by the same name as the Republican incumbent, Sen. Dan Sullivan, R-Alaska, in the Alaska Senate race.

Trump made the statement in an interview with Fox News after a campaign rally in Alaska on Tuesday night. He suggested the second Sullivan's presence in the race was a "hoax" by Democrats to siphon voters away from the Republican candidate.

"We are looking, I can't say federal, but we are looking into it. It's a disgrace. We have, I call him the real Dan Sullivan, a great senator from Alaska. And in the race, they put somebody named Dan Sullivan who knows nothing about politics. His name happens to be Dan Sullivan. They even wanted to change his middle initial, which was different. They wanted to make it an S so that it could be exactly correct. I think it's just terrible that they did it," Trump said.
SEEING DOUBLE: SECOND DAN SULLIVAN ADVANCES, SETTING UP BIZARRE ALASKA SENATE BALLOT
"And actually, he got two points or something in the primary. The real Dan Sullivan won it, but ... It's a terrible thing. It's another hoax by the Democrats," he added.

Trump also weighed in on the gubernatorial race in Alaska, where he has endorsed GOP candidate Bernadette Wilson. Other GOP candidates have been hangers-on in the race, despite Wilson winning the primary.
Trump called on her Republican competitor, Dave Bronson, to drop out of the race.

"He doesn't have to, but he should, because, frankly, he lost in the primary by substantial numbers to Bernadette. And I'm not involved that much in, you know, Alaska politics, other than I want to see Dan and Nick get in. But she won in the primaries, and the others should have dropped out. So now you have three Republicans running against one Democrat. And I don't like that. I don't like those odds very much. But there, she's great, and maybe she'll get in, but I thought I had an obligation to endorse her," Trump said.
Trump went on to criticize the Democrat in the race, Mary Peltola , following her criticism that Sullivan had voted in favor of the war in Iran.
GOP SENATOR, EX-HOUSE DEM EMERGE FROM ALASKA’S ‘JUNGLE PRIMARY’ DESPITE FAR-LEFT MEDDLING
The president argued Americans understand that increased prices at the pump are a "small price to pay" to prevent Tehran from obtaining a nuclear weapon .

"Can you imagine if they attacked our cities, and they attacked places where we are, including right here in Alaska? You would see turmoil far greater. We have a lot of oil flowing right now in the almost strait, we control it. The war is going to be over very, very soon. We're going to have a big victory very shortly. Very, very shortly, and oil is going to come way, way down. Gasoline is going to come down to where it was before," Trump said.

"I had it down to $1.85 a gallon in some places like Iowa and a lot of places, actually. And I think we're going to maybe even top those numbers. So you're going to see it. But most importantly, Iran, the number-one state sponsor of terror, will never have a nuclear weapon. If they had one, you might not be standing here right now," he added.

articles.headline: Zelenskyy sits down with NPR. And, Pope Leo diagnosed with lung cancer
keyFacts: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy told NPR that the Trump administration warned it could cut intelligence-sharing unless Ukraine stops drone strikes on Russian oil refineries.
The Vatican announced that Pope Leo XIV was diagnosed with lung cancer after doctors successfully removed the lower lobe of his right lung during surgery.
President Trump ousted Kimberly Guilfoyle as his ambassador to Greece following allegations that she attempted to profit from her position.
body: Zelenskyy sits down with NPR. And, Pope Leo diagnosed with lung cancer
Good morning. You're reading the Up First newsletter. Subscribe here to get it delivered to your inbox, and listen to the Up First podcast for all the news you need to start your day.
Today's top stories

In an interview with NPR, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said that the Trump administration warned it could cut intelligence-sharing with Ukraine unless Ukrainian forces halt long-range drone strikes on Russian oil refineries. Zelenskyy said the administration's decision to lift sanctions on Russian diesel won't lower fuel prices and refuted President Trump's claim that Ukraine caused the price to spike, instead pointing to the war in Iran. This interview comes as Russia's full-scale invasion approaches its five-year mark.

- 🎧 Zelenskyy says that every piece of intelligence is crucial for Ukraine, as stopping ballistic missiles is a top priority, NPR's Joanna Kakissis tells Up First. Missiles have killed dozens of Ukrainians, including more than 20 people recently in an apartment building in Pryluky. Zelenskyy recounted to Kakissis visiting a wounded girl in the hospital whose father died in the attack, though she didn't know it. Zelenskyy says he feels the impact of each attack deeply. Last week, Trump said that Russia and Ukraine agreed to halt some strikes on energy sites. Zelenskyy said he would comply if Russia did the same. Two hours after Trump's announcement, Russia targeted a Ukrainian power plant, and the strikes have continued.

Pope Leo XIV has been diagnosed with lung cancer following surgery to remove a growth from his lung, the Vatican announced. Doctors at Gemelli Hospital in Rome removed the lower lobe of the 71-year-old Pope's right lung during a successful procedure that lasted about 90 minutes. Post-surgery analysis confirmed the diagnosis of lung adenocarcinoma.

- 🎧 NPR's Scott Detrow says that lung experts he has spoken with are optimistic about the Pope's condition, based on Vatican statements. Dr. Vin Gupta from the University of Washington says that doctors' actions suggest that they caught the cancer early, suggesting it hasn't spread. If that is the case, this diagnosis may not impact his lifespan. The Pope will stay hospitalized for several days, and his schedule is cleared for at least a week. Detrow has spoken to several of the Pope's friends, who have been in contact with him and say he remains responsive and in good spirits.

Trump has ousted Kimberly Guilfoyle as his ambassador to Greece. She was a prominent MAGA figure and the former fiancée of his oldest son. Guilfoyle faced unflattering allegations that she was trying to profit from her position, which she denies. The Wall Street Journal reported a series of questionable actions by Guilfoyle last month. One incident involved her asking a Trump donor for $100,000 to settle a credit card bill, promising to use her connections within the administration in return.

- 🎧 Trump called for Guilfoyle's resignation yesterday, citing unfavorable media coverage. The president mentioned he hadn't even spoken to her before she announced her departure on X. NPR's Michele Kelemen spoke to Gregory Meeks, the ranking Democrat on the House Foreign Affairs Committee, who said that her resignation doesn't equate to accountability and urged Congress and the inspector general to investigate her actions and the possible misuse of taxpayer funds. Meeks added that serving as a U.S. ambassador is a position of public trust, not a business opportunity. Guilfoyle has defended her commitment to advancing Trump's America First agenda in Greece and vowed to defend her name, reputation and integrity.

A federal judge ruled late yesterday that Trump cannot bar news organizations from covering him at the White House because he doesn't like their coverage, at least until a formal trial concludes. U.S. District Court Judge Timothy J. Kelly found that Trump's decision to exclude more than 70 journalists from CNN, MS NOW, and Politico violated their free speech and due process rights. Both rights are enshrined in the Bill of Rights of the U.S. Constitution.
On the ground

The results of the 2026 midterm elections will shape the final two years of President Trump's second term and serve as a precursor to the 2028 general election. This month, Morning Edition is reporting from six states that could change the balance of power in Washington.

This week, Morning Edition's A Martínez traveled to the reliably red state of Texas. The cost of living is a major concern for many voters here. Ground beef hit a record high of about $7/lb in August, which is around $1.50 more than when Trump returned to office. In Floresville, Texas, Martínez spoke with a fourth-generation farmer and rancher who raises beef cattle about the challenges he is facing. Listen to what he had to say.
Martínez also spoke with residents about what is on their minds ahead of Election Day. Hear more about:
- 🎧 How the redistricting battle launched by Texas Republicans could alter Latino representation.

- 🎧 The impact that the Trump administration's immigration policies have had on a Texas border town, and why a conservative pastor near the end of his life shifted his vote and dedicated his life to supporting migrants.
- 🎧 Why the Senate and gubernatorial races are unusually competitive this year.

Follow the reporting: North Carolina and Georgia coverage airs Oct. 20, followed by reporting from Ohio and Michigan. You can follow along on Morning Edition, NPR.org, in the NPR app and in this newsletter.
Behind the story
by Anthony Kuhn, International Correspondent
To report on Lady Gaga's ad for the FamilyMart convenience store chain, the first thing I had to do was watch the video of it.

Gaga plays the part of a store worker dancing through the aisles in a leather uniform and platform shoes. To me, she looked like a high priestess of camp, boogying through a temple of retail efficiency to a mad techno beat.
It wasn't just the wild style that hooked me. It was also the confluence of culture and commerce in Japan.

The issue of Japan's aging society and its shrinking workforce are an inescapable part of life in Japan, and foreign workers are an inevitable part of the solution. FamilyMart's ad leverages Lady Gaga's non-conformist pop persona to appeal to an increasingly diverse workforce, a retail analyst explained to me.

Konbinis, as convenience stores are called in Japan, are also an inescapable part of life there. They function as a deli, post office, copy shop, bank, tax office and Ticketmaster all rolled into one. That's because it's cheaper for the government and businesses to offer these services through the konbinis than to run their own.

Another draw is the crazy fresh food, delivered to the stores several times a day. When I'm on assignment in Tokyo, I'm often on deadlines, so I head straight for the konbini onigiri (rice balls) with salmon, tofu and seaweed salad and mochi for dessert. It would be nice to have time for a proper meal, but until I do, I'm not too badly off living the konbini lifestyle.
Give the segment a listen, at your convenience!
3 things to know before you go
- A federal judge has temporarily stopped the Trump administration from cutting more trees at East Potomac Golf Links after it cut down hundreds with little notice.

- NPR has announced the winners of the Student Podcast Challenge after reviewing nearly 1,500 submissions from 42 states and Washington, D.C. Check out the grand prize winner for middle school, who talks about her dyslexia, and for high school, who discusses an important family memory.
- Cheese company Sargento has updated American cheese, also known in the industry as processed pasteurized cheese, to reflect modern eating habits by introducing a natural version. (via KCUR)
